summary: Debunks the buyer-favorable myth: seller pays margin via collateral (no cash), wins by probability, and can hedge/adjust; buyer is a lottery ticket. Small capital buys, big capital sells.
lessons: For every option bought one is sold - if buying were strictly better, no seller would exist.
Seller pays margin as collateral (FDs/shares), so cash outlay can be near zero; buyer pays premium in cash.
Probability decides long-run winners: buyer wins in only one of five market scenarios, seller in most.
Sellers can adjust/hedge a losing position (short futures, sell calls); a buyer has no equivalent fix.

strategies.name: Collateral-funded option selling (framework)
strategies.construction: Sell options against collateral: bank FD, shares, mutual funds or bank guarantee pledged to the broker
strategies.numbers: Buyer pays 2,000-3,000 premium cash vs seller margin ~80,000-90,000 (as stated) but pledgable in kind
strategies.best_regime: Traders with large capital seeking steady returns
strategies.adjustments: Losing short can be adjusted via short futures or selling calls on the other side
strategies.risks: Margin calls on booked losses; losses can exceed premium received if unhedged

quotes: With limited capital, if you want unlimited profit, either the risk is very high or the probability is very low.
Option selling does not need extraordinary skill, you just need to have extraordinary capital.

summary: Consolidation with negative bias after US tariff news (Dow -900 intraday). Private banks, Reliance, HDFC dragged; mid/small caps outperformed. FII sold ~1,600cr; October FII selling crossed 30,000cr - highest month since January 2008. India VIX near 21. Bank Nifty flat for 5 weeks despite 500+ point daily swings.
lessons: High VIX with flat close-to-close moves means violent intraday swings inside a range - the option seller's regime map.

summary: RBI-government standoff (Section 7, governor resignation reports) knocked Nifty to 10,100; Coal India FPO (4,500cr + 9,000cr greenshoe) added supply. Government clarification fueled short covering: Nifty +300, Bank Nifty +600 from lows; HDFC Bank +5%. India VIX crashed 14% intraday. FII sold only 193cr; DII bought 1,120cr.
lessons: Max-OI put strikes show option sellers' conviction levels about support.

summary: Positive open on Ease of Doing Business rank jump, crude fall and L&T results; rupee appreciated on RBI-government resolution, pressuring IT. HDFC results +50-60 then profit booking; Nifty high ~10,450. VIX fell 3%; puts fell even with Nifty only -6. FII bought +200cr, DII sold >500cr. Thesis: double bottom near 10,000.
lessons: Falling VIX on a flat/down day explains why option premiums decay on both sides - a seller's tailwind.

summary: Global rout: Dow -1,000 over two days, all S&P sectors down, crude -7%, cryptos down. Crude's fall a blessing for the rupee; banks outperformed while Reliance dragged (-2.5 to -3%). FII sold >1,000cr cash on consecutive days. OI map: 10,500 PE / 11,000 CE; Bank Nifty expiry range 26,000-26,500; he sold both wings.
lessons: Option sellers can pre-commit to an expiry range from max-OI strikes and hedge the tails.

summary: Quiet consolidation ahead of the Trump-Xi G20 dinner in Argentina - a true binary event. Expects no final trade outcome, only talk announcements. Private banks (Kotak, SBI) and Reliance held the tape; FII net sellers, DII heavy buyers. His book: downside butterfly plus upside call ratio, positions light ahead of events.
lessons: Before binary events, sell structure (butterfly/ratio) instead of naked direction and keep size light.

summary: Foundational primer: calls and puts taught through a Virat Kohli cricket-betting analogy and a business-profit story; explains strike, premium, expiry and how expectation moves premium before price does.
lessons: An option is asymmetric betting: buyer risks only the premium; seller pays 1:1 per point beyond the strike.
Premium moves on expectation, not just price - a batter racing toward a century raises the 'premium' before the century exists.
Call buyers profit when market rises, put buyers when it falls - but volatility and time decay can still turn a right view into a loss.
Buyers can exit before expiry; profit-taking need not wait for settlement.
quotes: The expectation will shoot up... though he has not hit the century, the premium rises as he scores more runs.

summary: Systematic demolition of the three buyer advantages (low premium, limited risk, unlimited reward): collateral funding, 20% win probability, profit-booking dilemma, and the lottery/robbery framing of risk-reward-probability.
lessons: 'Limited risk, unlimited reward' always pairs with very low probability (lottery) or very high risk (robbery).
Seller's real risk is bounded by the trading capital actually deployed, not theoretical unlimited loss.
Buyer psychology fails at profit booking - 10 to 50 to zero on expiry day; seller's capped profit removes greed.
Nifty never moves far enough in a month for 'unlimited' to matter; few hundred points is the real range.
quotes: Every day I switch on TV, I find some people die of accidents. Are we going to say getting out of the house is unlimited risk?
The probability of winning for an option buyer is less than 20%.

summary: VIX masterclass during COVID: definition (expected 30-day movement, not a fear gauge that must rise in falls), sqrt-12 monthly conversion, advance-decline check for why VIX fell on a falling day, and strike placement beyond the expected move.
lessons: VIX measures expected one-month movement; it can fall in a falling market when the fall is narrow (heavyweights only, breadth positive).
Monthly expected move = VIX / sqrt(12); place short strikes beyond that band (example: VIX 60 -> ~17% band).
VIX is derived from option prices - the straddle premium is a live cross-check of the VIX-implied range.
High VIX favors sellers who keep distance; low VIX means the market is priced for calm and strikes must come closer.

strategies.name: VIX-based expected-move strangle placement
strategies.construction: Sell puts below spot - (VIX/sqrt(12))% and calls above spot + (VIX/sqrt(12))%
strategies.numbers: VIX 60 -> monthly band ~17.3%; spot 8,000 -> sell puts below ~6,500, calls above ~9,500; May 8,000 straddle ~1,600 (~20% for 37 trading days)
strategies.best_regime: Elevated VIX (crisis); recompute daily as VIX moves
strategies.adjustments: None stated - guideline framing, refresh band as VIX changes
strategies.risks: Band is statistical, not a wall; theta/other factors shift premiums; violent moves can exceed the band

quotes: It is not necessary that when the market goes down, the VIX has to go up - VIX is all about the perception of the market over the next one month.

summary: Explains the violent up-move anomaly: strangle sellers trapped by a ~10% rally are forced to buy back far puts to free margin and re-sell closer strikes - creating put-premium distortion. Never deploy all margin; short strangle is the most dangerous strategy.
lessons: In violent moves, premiums behave abnormally because losing-side sellers are forced to square up and roll - not because the market 'should' behave that way.
Never deploy all margin in a strangle; spare cash lets you sell closer strikes without buying back the far leg at the worst price.
Short strangle is called the most dangerous strategy - unlimited one-sided loss with both legs naked.
Margin-release mechanics (square far leg, sell nearer leg) explain bid-ask distortions during panics.

strategies.name: Strangle roll-under-stress mechanics
strategies.construction: Short 9,000CE + 7,000PE written Friday around spot 8,000; on a violent rally, buy back 7,000PE (releasing margin) and sell 7,500/8,000PE instead
strategies.numbers: Legs 1,000 points either side of spot; roll targets 500-1,000 points closer
strategies.best_regime: After violent directional moves when the losing leg must be repositioned
strategies.adjustments: Roll the losing short leg closer using either spare cash (preferred) or margin released by squaring the far leg
strategies.risks: Forced buyback at inflated premiums; whipsaw if the market reverses immediately

quotes: Always remember, when markets move violently, do not expect option premiums to behave in the normal course.

summary: P&L transparency episode: ~50% return in six April-2020 sessions driven by VIX collapse 86->50 plus a bullish view; demonstrates position-level losses coexisting with net profit, and strike/expiry diversification; explicitly warns viewers not to copy the risk.
lessons: High-VIX regimes let low-volume sellers earn outsized returns as VIX collapses - the profit engine is vega plus view, not volume.
Spread risk across many strikes (6,500 through 8,500 puts) and multiple expiries (weekly/May/June) - never concentrate one strike.
Position-level losses (up to ~1.75 lakh single positions) coexist with net profit - judge the portfolio, not each leg.
Never copy aggressive sizing: capital and risk appetite differ; matching the trade without matching the capital is ruinous.

strategies.name: Strike-and-expiry put ladder (illustrative, high risk)
strategies.construction: Sold puts at 6,500 / 7,000 / 7,300 / 7,400 / 7,500 / 7,800 / 8,500 across weekly, May and June expiries; small stock-option positions (IndusInd 800 qty @22.52; ~2,300PE on a NBFC stock, 4 lots @220)
strategies.numbers: Capital ~95 lakh -> ~45 lakh profit in 6 sessions (~50%); sold Jun 7,000PE @475, May 6,500PE @210 (closed 80), May 7,000PE @324 (closed 117)
strategies.best_regime: Extreme high VIX with stabilizing market (COVID April 2020)
strategies.adjustments: Laddered entries across expiries instead of single-strike concentration
strategies.risks: Aggressive directional sizing; a renewed crash through the ladder strikes would produce large losses; explicitly not replicable by retail

quotes: We also lose. What matters is whether, at the end of the day, the profits are more than the losses.
I have sold 6,500, 7,000, 7,500, 7,300, 7,400, 7,800, 8,500 - I spread my risk across strike prices and across expiry dates.

summary: Teaches the cash-secured put end to end: sell a put at a strike you are happy to own, collect premium, take delivery if assigned. Shows live positions (Bajaj Finance, IndusInd, Nifty puts) and a claimed Rs.45 lakh FY21 profit in three weeks.
lessons: Sell puts only at prices where you are happy to take delivery - the premium is income, the strike is your target entry.
Far-month puts pay large premiums and give delivery intent when the market reaches your buy zone.
Squaring off and buying in the open market is usually cleaner than waiting for physical settlement.

strategies.name: Cash Secured Put
strategies.construction: Sell a put at the strike where you want to own the stock; keep the full cash ready for delivery
strategies.numbers: Bajaj Finance 1800PE sold at Rs.100 (2 lots, Rs.50,000 collected); Nifty Apr 7500PE ~Rs.57; Dec-2020 6000PE ~Rs.200; ~Rs.19 lakh premium collected; claimed Rs.45 lakh FY21 P&L in 3 weeks
strategies.best_regime: Sideways-to-up markets, or when you want a lower entry price in a quality stock
strategies.adjustments: Square off the put and buy shares in the open market instead of physical delivery; exit any time before expiry
strategies.risks: Profit capped at premium; stock can fall far below strike; requires full cash backing of the strike

quotes: If you are prepared to take delivery and the price does not fall below the strike, every month you can be making money.
When you square off and buy from the market, it is as good as buying at strike minus premium collected.

summary: Replies to ROI/margin critics by showing scale: ~23 lakh quantity through one broker in a day, about 1.5% of the 8700PE contract's day volume; argues absolute profit and capital-handling skill matter more than percentage ROI.
lessons: Absolute profit matters more than ROI percentage - the real skill is the amount of capital you can handle.
With intraday limits the deployed capital is the broker's; judge the trade by loss potential, not ROI optics.
All charges are computed on premium, so selling low-premium options keeps costs proportionally tiny.
quotes: I do not look at open interest. I create open interest.
If you are looking only at ROI, nobody can beat begging - the return is infinite.

summary: Pre-results Infosys structure: short straddle at 650, converted to an iron fly with long 720CE/580PE wings, wings financed by selling double quantity of 750CE and 550PE. Payoff: max ~Rs.3.58 lakh (15%) at 650, protection zones 710/590.
lessons: Enter earnings trades the day before results and exit once the event resolves; hold further only with a stop-loss.
Finance protective wings by selling double quantity of farther strikes so the hedge costs nothing from pocket.
A naked short straddle is high risk; the same view becomes limited-risk when converted to an iron fly.

strategies.name: Infosys earnings iron fly with financed wings
strategies.construction: Sell 650CE + 650PE (5 lots); buy 720CE + 580PE; sell 2x 750CE (10 lots) and 2x 550PE to finance the wings
strategies.numbers: 650CE @31, 650PE @27.50, 720CE @7.35, 580PE @8.40, 750CE @4, 550PE @4.46; max profit ~Rs.3.58 lakh (~15%) if Infosys closes at 650; protection 710 up / 590 down
strategies.best_regime: Results eve with elevated implied volatility
strategies.adjustments: Exit after results or keep far wings with a stop-loss; watch volatility crush
strategies.risks: Beyond 750/550 the financing legs turn the risk unlimited again; overnight gap risk

quotes: This is the second strategy, iron fly - a limited risk strategy.
I do not want to pay from my pocket to buy the 720 call, so I sold double quantity of the 750 call.

summary: Post-mortem of the Infosys earnings structure: stock fell ~3% after results yet every leg netted a profit - total Rs.8.95/share (Rs.10,740 per lot). Walks through margin with hedging benefits (~Rs.7.24 lakh) and the scaling argument for large capital.
lessons: Hedged option combos earn margin benefits - selling both sides costs far less margin than the sum of separate legs.
Option selling is about safely handling large capital, not about flashy percentage returns.
Exit near legs once the event resolves; keep far wings only with a stop-loss.

strategies.name: Post-earnings leg-by-leg review of the hedged straddle
strategies.construction: 650CE/PE sold; 720CE/580PE long; 750CE/550PE sold 2x - each leg marked after the results
strategies.numbers: Total +8.95/share = Rs.10,740 per lot (lot 1200); margin ~Rs.7.24 lakh after benefits for the 5-lot structure; ~1.5% in a day; projected ~4% in two weeks
strategies.best_regime: Immediately after results, when volatility crush pays all sold legs
strategies.adjustments: Closed the 650/720 and 650/580 pairs; kept 750CE/550PE with a stop-loss
strategies.risks: Far wings are effectively naked beyond 750/550

quotes: Option selling is not about making huge profit - it is all about handling the huge sum of money.
Though you pay 197,000 while placing the order, the next day the premium receivable is credited back to your ledger.

summary: Contrasts results timing and IV: Infosys declares after hours (ATM IV ~67) while IndusInd declares intraday (ATM IV ~140). Plan: sell May-series 400CE+400PE straddle, hedge with current-month 500CE/300PE; net ~Rs.94.55/share (Rs.37,800/lot) on ~Rs.60,000 margin.
lessons: For high-IV stocks, sell the next-month straddle - richer premium with relatively smaller risk - and hedge with current-month wings.
Results timing matters: after-hours declarations carry gap risk, intraday declarations let you react.
ATM IV doubling between a quiet IT major and a volatile bank shows why event trades must be sized by IV, not by price.

strategies.name: IndusInd Bank earnings hedged straddle (May series)
strategies.construction: Sell May 400CE @62 + 400PE @52; buy current-month 500CE @4.25 + 300PE @5.25 as protection
strategies.numbers: Net premium ~Rs.94.55/share = Rs.37,800 per lot; margin ~Rs.60,000; >50% return if IndusInd closes near 400 at May expiry
strategies.best_regime: High-IV stock ahead of results; next-month premium rich relative to risk
strategies.adjustments: Exit opportunity after the results; avoid holding the full month
strategies.risks: Very large move beyond the wings; one month is a long time in trading

quotes: One month is a very long time in trading.
In IndusInd, the long strangle can be in the current month to reduce the cost.

summary: Franklin Templeton wound up six debt schemes (~30,000 crore) after redemption pressure; explains the butterfly effect - HNI option sellers had pledged these debt funds as collateral, exchanges zeroed collateral value, forcing liquidation that hit Friday's market.
lessons: Option sellers pledge debt funds/FDs/liquid funds as collateral instead of paying cash margin
Exchange collateral haircuts can jump to 100% overnight - pledged positions then force-liquidate
Whatever happens anywhere in the world, the stock market feels it first
quotes: Remember, whatever happens anywhere in the world, the first one to be affected will be the stock market.

summary: Monthly P&L review: April profit 66.3 lakh on ~95 lakh starting capital after 45 lakh in first two weeks; attributes windfall to India VIX collapse 80-85 to ~40 and Nifty clearing the 38.2% Fibonacci retracement (9300-9400) toward 9900-10000; March also +50 lakh selling calls.
lessons: High collapsing VIX plus a clear directional view is where option sellers make windfall profits - not repeatable monthly
Know when to exit: he closed nearly all positions after the Fibonacci target hit
Markets factor in known bad news (efficient market) - shorting after visible bad news is how traders get squeezed
A trader can profit in a falling market and lose in a rising one - the view matters, not the market's direction

strategies.name: Put-selling ladder in collapsing-VIX rebound
strategies.construction: Sold puts across strikes from ~6,100 to 9,000 during April 2020 recovery
strategies.numbers: April profit 66,30,478 on ~95L capital; VIX 80-85 -> 55-60 -> ~40; June 9000PE sold at 500, closed 180
strategies.best_regime: post-crash VIX collapse with market refusing to make new lows
strategies.adjustments: not detailed in this episode
strategies.risks: windfall not repeatable; VIX normalizes; requires conviction view

quotes: A trader can make profit even in a falling market and lose money even in a rising market - it is the view of the trader that is more important.
Markets are irrational and can continue to be irrational until you go bankrupt.

summary: Live bullish Nifty trade: after booking profit on naked 9000/8700 puts, builds a call-ratio (long 9400CE, short 2x 9800CE, short 10000CE) funded by selling weekly calls, showing basket-order execution and payoff math; also reviews a May-4 June-series 9500 short straddle up 8.5% in six sessions.
lessons: Success needs two things: an edge (view/skill) and a hedge.
Sell far OTM calls to finance a directional long - no out-of-pocket premium, capped upside is the accepted cost.
A short straddle in a quiet regime can yield high-single-digit monthly returns on margin.
Bank Nifty read-through: one big bank's results miss drags peers awaiting their own results.

strategies.name: Call ratio spread (financed directional)
strategies.construction: Long 1x 9400CE; short 2x 9800CE; short 1x 10000CE (300/600/300 qty), plus weekly far-OTM call sales to offset net debit
strategies.numbers: 9400CE ~219; 9800CE ~80; 10000CE ~45; net ~-4300 before weekly sales (~+2800 after); max profit ~1,15,000 at 9800 expiry; loss begins ~10,080
strategies.best_regime: Mildly bullish, expect stay below written strikes
strategies.adjustments: Promised follow-up through expiry; weekly-call sales used to neutralize debit
strategies.risks: Unlimited above 10,080 (net short top strike); upside capped at 9800 zone

quotes: If you want to be successful in the stock market, you need two things: edge and hedge.

summary: Q&A clarifying mechanics: buy/sell quantities are always equal (TV 'delivery buying' is interpretation); futures settle daily via MTM while option sellers' margin = span + premium value, rising with the option price; NSE uses a 10% risk-free rate in IV; June-2020 hedged margins ~one-third of naked; expiry settlement uses last-half-hour weighted average, not last traded price.
lessons: Futures: daily MTM cash transfer. Options: buyer pays premium once; seller's margin floats with the option's price.
Expiry settlement price is the weighted average of the last half hour - an ITM option can expire worthless despite a favorable last traded price.
Hedged option positions carry roughly one-third the margin of naked shorts (June 2020 regime).
Crowd consensus is dangerous: markets are structured so only the minority profits.

summary: ₹20 lakh crore package spiked hopes then sold off; FIIs accelerated selling (>2,000 crore Friday; >15,000 crore in 3 weeks); heavyweight banks fell 10-20% in May (Kotak -20%); VIX falling and PCR 0.8 say bottom near; range 9,000-9,500.
lessons: Falling VIX in a falling market means the remaining downside is limited.
PCR ~0.8 + put OI close to spot + call OI far away = sellers confident, bottom-building pattern.

summary: Q&A: age-percentage debt rule and SIP/SWP for a retiree down 35%; short straddle as favorite strategy; ITM stock options must be squared off (physical delivery) while index options settle in cash at the half-hour VWAP; prefer LEAPS for low-monitoring office-goers; square off OTM options at 5 paise for clean tax statements; India lacks hedge funds because AIF Cat III has no tax pass-through; never sell options expiring the next day.
lessons: Keep roughly your-age-percent in debt; deploy lump sums via SIP, withdraw via SWP.
Trade indices, not stocks: ITM stock options that lapse trigger physical delivery; index options are cash-settled.
Sell options with enough time to expiry - next-day expiry invites gap risk you cannot hedge after the fact.
Square off even worthless shorts for clean broker statements and smoother income-tax scrutiny.

summary: Monthly trade review: ~10 lakh May profit on ~95 lakh capital (76 lakh total in two months, ~80%). Dissects three large losses (Nifty future and two call options, ~12 lakh combined), a profitable ratio spread, cash-secured puts in ICICI/HDFC Bank, and corrects an earlier mistaken March figure.
lessons: Never benchmark one month against the last - the market 'is like God; take what it gives'. Expectation inflation destroys discipline.
Index-only trading survives regime changes: when SEBI raised stock-option margins from June 2020, index positions kept the margin edge.
Patience through adverse moves rescued the IndusInd straddle: sold at 105, expired with ~80% return despite mid-trade criticism.
Cash-secured puts with genuine willingness to take delivery convert fear into income.

strategies.name: Cash-secured puts (ICICI 300PE, HDFC 840PE)
strategies.construction: Sell puts below market with full cash set aside for delivery
strategies.numbers: +33,000 ICICI and +28,000 HDFC in May 2020
strategies.best_regime: moderately bullish with stocks near support
strategies.adjustments: take delivery if assigned; roll if view changes
strategies.risks: sharp breakdown below strike forces delivery at loss

strategies.name: Put ratio spread (9100PE bought / 8500PE sold)
strategies.construction: Long lower put, short further-OTM puts
strategies.best_regime: mildly bearish to flat
strategies.adjustments: close short side on breakdown
strategies.risks: accelerated loss beyond short strikes

quotes: People lose money because they do not want to lose money - they expect zero-loss calls, which is impossible.

summary: First follow-up of a long-term Reliance position managed through futures plus options: bought May future at 1422, sold 1460 call, converted to straddles twice, rolled puts, and finished ~1.6 lakh profit versus ~35-40k unhedged, using under 5 lakh margin against a 15 lakh cash cost.
lessons: Hedging skill converts a 35-40k directional profit into ~1.6 lakh on the same view - the edge is in management, not prediction.
Fund long-term equity exposure with futures + collateral: park the cash-equivalent in interest-bearing debt instruments, trade on margin.
Wealth sequence: trade actively to compound, then convert to buy-and-hold - 'buy 1000 shares and forget it'.
Rollover cost is a regime signal: bearish markets roll cheap, bullish markets roll expensive.

strategies.name: Futures + rolling short straddle on a long-term holding
strategies.construction: Long monthly future; sell ATM calls; convert to straddles; roll puts lower as market falls (1460->1440); add 1520C
strategies.numbers: entry 1422, May-2020 series; +159,186 total vs ~35-40k unhedged; margin <=5 lakh vs 15 lakh cash
strategies.best_regime: long-term bullish holding with two-way volatility
strategies.adjustments: square and re-strike puts on reversals; roll future at ~1 point cost in bearish tape
strategies.risks: gap risk on naked legs; assignment/roll slippage

quotes: If you keep looking at the investment every day, the investment will not grow.

summary: Walks through SEBI's new margining on real examples: naked ATM options now ~1.0-1.3 lakh (up from 80-90k), but hedged spreads collapse to ~25-35k, cross-margined straddles to ~1.05 lakh, straddle-with-wings to ~45-55k, and an ITM put calendar under 30k - pushing traders toward hedged, index, defined-risk structures.
lessons: Under the new framework the margin system itself pays you to hedge: protection 200-300 points away cuts margin ~70%.
Cross-margining makes a short straddle cost little more than its single costlier leg - portfolio margin logic arrives in India.
Margin relief can seduce into over-sizing: four lots at 300-point risk recreates 1,200 points of exposure. Options trading is risk and position management, not strike selection.
Index exposure carries structurally lower margins (2% vs 3.5% exposure) - another argument to avoid stock options.

strategies.name: Hedged short option (spread)
strategies.construction: Sell 10,000C / buy 10,200C (200pt); variants 300-400pt
strategies.numbers: ~25,000-32,000 margin vs 80-90k naked; max risk = spread width
strategies.best_regime: any directional credit view
strategies.adjustments: roll wings as market trends
strategies.risks: max loss = width x lot; premium give-up

strategies.name: Short straddle with far wings
strategies.construction: Sell 9,500CE+9,500PE (July), buy 8,500PE+10,500CE (June weekly/next series)
strategies.numbers: margin ~45,000-55,000 after ~40-60k premium receivable; straddle premium >1,000 pts in July 2020
strategies.best_regime: high-IV months with distant wings affordable
strategies.adjustments: re-buy expired wings weekly
strategies.risks: gap through wings; weekly-wing rollover friction

strategies.name: ITM put calendar
strategies.construction: Sell 10,000PE current month, buy 10,000PE next month
strategies.numbers: margin <30,000
strategies.best_regime: neutral-to-mildly-bearish
strategies.adjustments: roll short leg at expiry
strategies.risks: fast rallies inflate long-leg decay loss

quotes: Options trading is not about which strike you sell - it is about risk management, margin management and position sizing.

summary: Q&A: debunks the short-selling 'ban' (practical cap ~500 crore plus margin), warns against 2008-pattern confirmation bias with the market at record highs, explains weekly-hedge rollover mechanics, options-vs-futures collateral treatment for MTM losses, margin-shortfall penalty slabs, and tells small-capital traders to avoid F&O.
lessons: Confirmation bias: when you want a crash you will find reasons - trade the market that is, not the pattern that 'should' repeat.
Options-seller MTM losses can be adjusted against collateral until booked; futures MTM must be paid in cash daily - know which instrument your capital can carry.
Squaring only the hedge leg instantly recreates a naked position: margin shortfall penalties run 0.5%/day (<1 lakh), 1%/day (>1 lakh), 5%/day from the sixth session.
There is no holy-grail directional formula in open interest - only guidelines plus experience.

strategies.name: Monthly short option + weekly protective hedge
strategies.construction: Sell far-month option; buy near-week option slightly OTM below breakeven; re-buy weekly
strategies.numbers: 9,000PE July sold (>100 premium), 8,900PE weekly bought; margin ~50,000 vs >1,00,000 unhedged
strategies.best_regime: credit selling with black-swan protection
strategies.adjustments: roll weekly wing; broker far-strike restrictions are the friction
strategies.risks: weekly wing expires worthless after rallies; rollover cost creep

quotes: People expect a crash because they studied 2008 - the market is not obliged to repeat anyone's pattern.

summary: Where-to-find tutorial: BSE results calendar, NSE company pages, and Moneycontrol's earnings page with expected announcement times (today/tomorrow only); explains IV-crush premium-selling around results; covers dividend/bonus/split calendars (Colgate 1600% dividend, GE Shipping, Sinclairs Hotel split) and aggregate earnings-season statistics.
lessons: Results timing is tradable information: premium sellers position minutes before announcements to capture the IV crush.
Expected result times are historical averages - only Infosys-class companies reliably hit them; build timing buffers into event trades.
Aggregate earnings statistics (share of companies beating, sales/profit growth) gauge whether a rally has fundamental breadth.
quotes: After results, implied volatility crashes - and the premium with it. That is the trade.

summary: Monthly accountability review: April-May +76 lakh on ~95 lakh capital, June lost ~1.2 lakh. Loss attribution: SBI trade -2 lakh (1.83 profit + 3.62 loss legs) and expiry-day sale of 10,000 calls at Rs 4 stopped out at Rs 23 for -2.82 lakh; without those two trades the month was +3.6 lakh.
lessons: Publish losses as loudly as wins: two high-risk trades turned a winning month into a small loss.
Expiry-day naked short calls sold at Rs 4 and stopped at Rs 23 show the tail risk of cheap-option selling.
Audit trades, not outcomes: removing the two worst decisions flips the month positive.

strategies.name: Expiry-day naked call selling (documented failure)
strategies.construction: Sell 10,000 CE on weekly expiry day (18 June 2020) in size at Rs 4
strategies.numbers: Entry ~Rs 4, stop-loss exit ~Rs 23, loss ~Rs 2.82 lakh

summary: Q&A batch: STT mechanics on sellers; time decay proportional to expiry (weekly day-1 = 20% of decay, expiry day = 100%); covered calls against physical shares still need full margin in India (no cash-F&O link) but a long futures leg reduces it to exposure margin; Bharat Bond 1 vs 2 (yield, premium, pledge-ability delay); NSE's six-month co-location ban on new contracts had just ended; bear/bull defined by 20% thresholds.
lessons: Time decay is proportional to remaining time: a one-week option loses ~20% of its value on day one, but ~100% on expiry day - expiry-day selling harvests decay that weekly sellers spread across days.
India charges full span+exposure margin on covered calls against demat shares (no cash-F&O link); holding a long future instead cuts the short call's span to zero - only exposure margin applies.
An instrument's 'maximum loss' framing: any investment can lose 100%; relative safety comes from the borrower (Bharat Bond lends only to public-sector enterprises).
Bond yields falling means older bonds trade at a premium (Bharat Bond 1 near 1080-1090 vs 1000 face); pledging older listed bonds can beat waiting for new issues to clear collateral approval.

summary: Foundational payoff teaching: selling a put is not buying a call. Regulatory asymmetry: curbs concentrated on option sellers (who post big margins) while option buyers - the actual gamblers - face no new restrictions.

summary: Two failure patterns: (1) the 'recover my loss' mindset - lost capital is sunk; a trader who learns to make 5 lakh/month will not quit after 'recovering', so trade fresh capital for decent returns; (2) gambler's fallacy - streaks don't change probabilities (Monte Carlo 1913: 26 reds; SBI falling 5 days says nothing about day 6). Nick Leeson's short strangle doubled down on 'it can't fall more' and Kobe earthquake destroyed Barings.
lessons: There is no such thing as recovering a loss - the money lost is tuition; treat remaining capital as fresh and target decent returns on it.
Gambler's fallacy: past streaks don't change next-day probabilities - a 5-day fall can continue on day 6.
Overbought can stay overbought and oversold oversold until you go bankrupt - never average/double down because 'it has fallen too much'.
quotes: If you have lost it, that is the fees you paid to learn the lesson. You start with fresh capital and a fresh mindset.
The overbought market can continue to be overbought. The oversold market can continue to be oversold until you go bankrupt.

summary: Growth-vs-value framework: high-dividend stocks trade sideways, so pair them with covered call selling. PFC profiled at ~₹90: P/E 3.31 (sector 21), P/B 0.37 (sector 1.81), >10% dividend yield (sector 0.85%), EPS ~₹27, government holds 56%. ITC averaging at ₹190 with ~3%/month from call selling; 2014 Rane-group picks yielded 8-10% and doubled.
lessons: High-dividend value stocks lack expansion story - pair them with systematic call selling instead of expecting multi-bagger moves.
Government's own revenue need forces PSU dividend continuity - a structural, not cyclical, yield anchor.
Covered calls on a 10% yielder can stack to ~25-30%/yr: dividend + option income + modest appreciation.

strategies.risks: Dividend cut risk; capital stays stagnant; call caps upside

quotes: Growth stocks reinvest their profit; value stocks pay it out because they don't know what else to do with it.

summary: SEBI's 25/25/25 multi-cap mandate is skewered with a cake-fairness analogy: top-500 market cap is ~80% large, 15% mid, 5% small, so proportional allocation should be 80/15/5. ~₹40,000 cr must rotate out of large caps, but no Nifty crash or smallcap melt-up follows: money can exit to non-Nifty large caps, funds may reclassify or seek extensions; US-listed Indian ADRs stayed green.
lessons: Rules that ignore market-cap proportions create bureaucratic flows, not fundamental repricing - expected rebalance trades often fail to materialize.
Rebalance fear prices in the wrong sellers: mandate money can rotate within the large-cap universe rather than out of it.
quotes: The cake was given to the whole family, so everyone must eat at least 25% - that is how fair the rule is.

summary: Monthly account review: ~₹1.49 cr profit YTD on ~₹1 cr capital (~150%) despite September's Bank Nifty -20% series; September itself only ~₹10L. Breakdown: Bank Nifty -₹5.5L, offset by hedging (+₹1.5L), ratio spread (+₹1.18L), ITC call-selling cost reduction (avg → ~₹171), Nifty (+₹1.4L), SBI (+₹38K); Sensex options -₹2L on illiquidity, hedged via Nifty. Lifestyle/charity offered as the real P&L verification heuristic.
lessons: In a -20% Bank Nifty month, hedged leg income (+ ratio spreads) against directional losses is what keeps the year at 150%.
Illiquid instruments (Sensex options then) force you to hedge in a liquid proxy (Nifty) - liquidity is a position-sizing input.
Aggressive call selling against a falling stock positions cuts cost basis faster than averaging alone (ITC to ~171).
Judge any claimed P&L by capital trajectory and lifestyle/charity over time - screenshots prove nothing.

strategies.construction: Directional futures/option legs + offsetting call hedges + occasional ratio spreads
strategies.numbers: Sep: BN -5.5L, hedges +1.5L, ratio +1.18L, ITC hedging +2.23L, Nifty +1.4L, SBI +38K, Sensex -2L → ~+10L on ~₹1 cr capital
strategies.best_regime: Volatile series where directional legs bleed
strategies.adjustments: Hedge in the next series when current-series data ends; move hedges to liquid proxies
strategies.risks: Illiquidity in new instruments (Sensex options) causes slippage and forced proxy hedging

quotes: Show me your one-year P&L - then look at the lifestyle and the charity, and you will know the truth.

summary: TCS buyback at an all-time high puzzles everyone; SEBI's 75% promoter cap caps it at ~10% of public holding, making the rumoured ₹3,000 tender worth only ~₹25-30 per 10 shares - yet sentiment added 7.5%. The trade: IV jumped 33→39 (IV percentile 64→82), so a 2700 short straddle (lot 300) made ~₹4,000 in one session on ~₹1.5L effective margin, targeting IV crush after results.
lessons: Buyback news pops are sentiment, not value: capped tender sizes make the arithmetic trivial - fade the euphoria, don't chase it.
IV percentile above 80 after a news pop is the classic short-straddle entry; the target is post-event IV crush, not direction.
Event-day option income needs margin math: premium received offsets posted margin (₹2.09L posted → ~₹1.5L effective).

strategies.construction: Sell ATM call + put same strike (2700, lot 300) into an IV spike

strategies.best_regime: Post-news elevated IV with binary event (results) next day
strategies.adjustments: Stop-loss on combined premium; exit into post-event IV collapse
strategies.risks: Gap through breakevens before crush; direction reversal

quotes: Don't go long or short on buyback news - sell the volatility the news created.

summary: Follow-up on earlier ITC recommendation (down 15%) explaining dividend-yield logic and hedged buying; then recommends BPCL citing divestment-delay correction, 4.65% dividend yield, inverse crude-oil relationship, and cash-secured-put or covered-call entry methods.
lessons: High-dividend stocks trade on yield logic: price falls raise the yield and attract institutions; expect patience, not quick upside
Never take leveraged futures positions on a dividend-yield recommendation - leverage changes the whole risk of the idea
Crude futures curve pricing years ahead near current spot implies oil-marketing companies face no input-cost shock
Two disciplined entries for dividend stocks: cash-secured puts (willing to take delivery) or cash shares plus covered calls

quotes: The more the price goes down, the more the dividend yield and the more institutions will show interest

summary: Week fell 400 points on European lockdowns and stalled stimulus; US election is the year's biggest event - contested outcome is the only bearish case; option premiums ultra-high (Bank Nifty ATM straddle ~2,000); advice: no directional trades until results; investors split 50/50 entries.
lessons: Markets want stability, not a party: any clear US winner lifts stocks; only a contested result sells them off.
Before binary events, keep traders out and let investors scale in 50/50 - insurance via position structure, not prediction.

summary: Futures = forward with price set at execution, not today; the sell-first-buy-later two-way capability vs cash market's one-way traffic; margin vs full payment (6 lakh exposure for ~1 lakh margin), lot sizes, expiry, and 10x leverage math; mark-to-market daily settlement explained with a 60,000 example.
lessons: Futures differ from forwards only in standardization: exchange-traded, margined, marked to market daily
The two-way traffic - sell first, buy later - is the futures market's structural edge over the cash market
Leverage cuts both ways: 10% margin makes a 1% stock move a 10% account move
Margin is a security deposit to the exchange, not a down payment to the seller; MTM settles daily
quotes: People who trade in futures have no future; people who trade in options have plenty of options

summary: Explains open interest from the seller's perspective: max-OI put = support and max-OI call = resistance because option SELLERS put up large margin (~1.2 lakh/lot vs a buyer's few thousand) and carry unlimited risk, so the market weights their conviction. Warns max-OI strikes migrate intramonth as sellers adjust.
lessons: Max-OI put strike is support only because sellers - who risk unlimited loss and post big margin - are concentrated there.
OI is contracts on both sides: every lot has a bear (buyer) and a bull (seller); analysts trust the seller's wallet.
Max-OI support/resistance is dynamic: after a 200-400 point fall, sellers shift OI to lower strikes.
Old vs new NSE sites differ only in shares-vs-contracts units (contract multiplier), not in data.
quotes: Options is a game where there is no level playing field - the buyer risks a few thousand, the seller risks lakhs with unlimited downside.

summary: Certainty premium: Congress certified Biden, Nasdaq outperformed. MSCI's surprise deletion of three Chinese telecoms sparked rotation rumors; actual FII cash buying was ₹6,000+ crore. Maruti +5%; TCS excellent results - watch Infosys ADR overnight to gauge Monday reaction; sold TCS 3,100 straddle ~₹190-200.
lessons: Use overnight ADR moves of listed peers to estimate next-day reactions to results.
Markets reward the removal of uncertainty more than the news itself.

summary: VIX rose ~10% in a rising market - taught that VIX is fear, not a directional signal; fear sat on the upside because call sellers were frightened. Sectoral rotation to autos (Tata Motors +10%). Introduced volume profile: Nifty support 14,100, Bank Nifty 31,300 for put selling. FII two-day flow >₹9,000 crore.
lessons: VIX measures fear, not direction - it can spike in rallies when option sellers sweat.
Anchor put-selling to volume-profile high-volume nodes, not round numbers.

summary: Consolidation with huge Wednesday volatility: Nifty swung -200/+150 to close +1 pt; banks outperformed on sub-5% CPI; HDFC Bank overtook Reliance as India's most valuable stock. Infosys/Wipro beat estimates, Infosys ADR +3-4% pre-market. FII bought ₹1,879 cr, DII sold ₹2,370 cr.
lessons: Consolidation with volatility is healthy - it defuses future corrections.
FIIs buy in bursts after pausing to bait short sellers; watch F&O positioning, not just cash.

summary: Nifty crossed 14,660→~14,780 then sold off; Bank Nifty −6% (−1,800) in two days. Reliance −2.5% just before results (profit booking rule); Bajaj Auto +10% on results. FIIs flipped sellers Friday after a buying month. OI: 14,000 PE ~₹30, 15,000 CE max. Budget (Feb 1) event risk. Range 14,000–14,800.
lessons: Stocks that run up sharply just before results get profit-booked into the print; weak ones short-cover.
Budget reaction depends on positioning: pessimism ahead can mean a post-event rally; euphoria leaves no room for misses.

summary: Full event-strategy masterclass: 10 years of budget data show close-to-close moves under 2% (only exception -3.26% was COVID, not budget); weekly ATM straddle priced ~3.3% move; long straddle/strangle usually loses. Better: put/call back spreads (max loss ~Rs 20k vs Rs 32k) and put/call ratio spreads or butterflies for defined risk.
lessons: Implied volatility is almost always higher than historical volatility - paying full straddle premium around events is structurally losing.
Across 10 budgets, Nifty never closed more than 2% from the prior close except the COVID-coinciding 2020 budget (-3.26%).

Even across seven major crises (Lehman, Greece, taper tantrum, China devaluation, demonetization+Trump, Brexit, Feb-2018 US flash crash), Nifty never gapped more than 400 points except Lehman and COVID; Bank Nifty max 1,200.
Back spreads cut max loss by a third versus long straddles and win big only on large moves in one direction.

quotes: The implied volatility is always higher than the historical volatility.

summary: GameStop week: Nifty ~14,500 Monday open to sub-13,600 Friday (−900 in 4 sessions) amid the US short squeeze; short sellers reportedly lost $20–43bn. Budget tomorrow — historically ≤2% moves, GST weakened its power. ICICI/Shree Cement weekend results. OI 13,000 PE / 14,000 CE. Range 13,000–14,000.
lessons: Don't fear the event everyone watches; fear the one nobody is positioned for (short squeeze vs budget).
In a firm bull market, 10–20% corrections are normal; up to 30% is within bull-market norms.

summary: 'Nirmala candle 2.0': post-budget Bank Nifty surged ~5,000 points in three days on ultra-low expectations - the FM was rewarded for what she did NOT tax. Global tailwinds (GameStop collapse freeing attention, stimulus hopes). Huge OI in 15,500 CE+PE straddle signaled the 15k push; 14,000 monthly support.
lessons: Event outcomes are judged against expectations - a market braced for the worst buys a neutral budget.
VIX rising during a rally is upside fear: sellers of calls are the ones sweating.

summary: Nifty ~15,150 ATH after six sessions from 13,600; doji fears buried by US stimulus progress. HCL Tech's $10bn milestone and employee bonus lifted IT; M&M results lifted autos; private banks at ATHs. Cautionary tales: the lady short at 9,000 (-₹35 lakh) and the ₹50,000 HNI-tip victim. India VIX still ~24 vs US ~20.
lessons: Know your risk and reward before shorting a bull market - the market can stay irrational longer than you can stay solvent.
SEBI registration is a qualification, not a competence certificate - tip-sellers exploit the halo.

summary: Exhaustion evidence: Nifty 13,600→15,257 in six sessions then doji close; Bank Nifty resisted 36,500-36,600 thrice with a huge 36,000 short straddle (weekly+monthly). Flagged consolidation 35,000-37,000 and Nifty 14,900-15,500 expiry range. NSE circular against brokers arranging margin funding; peak-margin penalty waiver plea; retold the 2012 15% flash crash.
lessons: Short straddles at round-number strikes mark where the crowd expects consolidation - trade the range they define.
A market that has doubled in a year and run 1,600 points in a week owes itself a rest - doji at highs is a topping signal, not a base.

summary: Crossfire consolidation: SGX +60 sold off in minutes; FII +₹1,787 cr vs DII -₹2,076 cr kept Bank Nifty whipsawing (+500/-1,000) with no net move. Wednesday-volatility pattern held. Showed straddle theta math (15,200 and 36,000 straddles earning 90-300+ points/day) and the Aditya Puri sale lesson: value vs valuation.
lessons: Insider sales are valuation events, not value verdicts - employees give value, the market gives valuation.
When FII and DII fight with equal force, expect huge intraday swings and flat closes - straddles, not direction, pay.

summary: India-China border disengagement news triggered Reliance short-covering (+4%); Dhirubhai Ambani's 1982 squeeze story - 'shorting Reliance is playing with fire'. Bank Nifty dragged by HDFC Bank (DIIs sell FII favorites). Posted his own 36,000 straddle P&L (~₹8 lakh on the day; ~₹16.55 lakh total) and debunked mean-reversion/gap-fill dogma.
lessons: Mean reversion and gap-fill are dogma, not law - no asset class obeys them mechanically.
Scoring against a heavily-shopped large cap (Reliance) is fighting history; position with the flow, size the risk.

summary: Consolidation day: Nifty flat (-10) while Bank Nifty outperformed (+200, crossed 36,000). Focus on falling India VIX (two straight -4% days), Bank Nifty 36,000 straddle printing ~4% return in two sessions, strong CPI/IIP data, and Nifty futures trading in discount as a big-move tell.
lessons: Falling VIX into declines signals consolidation, not panic; futures discount often precedes a bigger directional move.
Open-interest changes (put writing at 35,500 Bank Nifty, call writing 15,200-15,300) reveal intraday institutional intent.

summary: Flat Nifty (-1.25 pt) after dream run; Bank Nifty hugely volatile (ICICI 680 high to 658 close). Core content: collateral mechanics explainer - pledging Bharat Bond (EBB ETF)/shares gives margin limits only; collateral pays margins (option selling, futures), never cash purchases; futures MTM losses need cash, option MTM can use collateral.
lessons: Collateral limits can fund margins only - never cash-market purchases; futures MTM losses must be paid in cash.
A ~160-point straddle premium means the large sellers expect a tight range for two sessions.

summary: Fourth straight DII-heavy selling session, yet thesis holds: correction not reversal. Top six Nifty gainers all PSU (ONGC, GAIL, BPCL, IOC, NTPC, Coal India); mid/small caps rose while only index heavyweights fell (HDFC twins + ICICI + RIL = 70 of 90-pt drop). Singapore highway-as-runway analogy for attacking holdings you depend on.
lessons: When heavyweights fall but breadth improves (PSU, midcaps up), the fall is rotation - not a market-wide exit.
15,000 put rose only 7-8 rupees on a -90 point day: time decay is the seller's friend in corrections.

summary: Global rate-scare profit booking: two perspectives on rising yields (2003–07 Sensex 7× despite rate hikes; crude $10→$150). Friday bottomed 14,900; last hour +100/+400 with no institutional support (FII +₹100 cr). 15,000 straddle ₹260–270; March OI heavy 14,000 PE. Bearish only below 14,700. Range 14,800–15,500-ish.
lessons: Rising rates have two readings — demand-driven inflation is good for profits; but yields also pull money from equities. Hold both views.
Mid/small caps and PSUs holding up while large caps sell = selling is positioning, not distribution.

summary: February series ends: Nifty 13,600→15,450→14,650→~15,100; Bank Nifty round trip 30,000→37,700→<35,000→+2,200 snap-back. March OI map: 14,000 max put / 16,000 max call; smart-money 15,000 straddle ~750 pts (implied 14,200-15,800). Explains FII +29,000cr print as promoter FDI→FII category-switch artifact, not real buying.
lessons: Max-OI strikes define the market's expected range; straddle premium quantifies it.
Raw FII flows can mislead - promoter-category switches create phantom single-day buying spikes.

summary: One-way bloodbath from open: Bank Nifty -5% (~2,000 pts), Nifty -4%, all 50 Nifty stocks red for the first time in a long while, close at day low. India GDP Q3FY21 0.4% vs 0.5% expected; rupee depreciated over a rupee - flagged as an FII-out tell. Premiums extreme: sold Bank Nifty 29,000PE & 40,000CE near 100+, weekly 15,800CE (1,300 away) at 6.
lessons: Rupee depreciation during a fall is a fingerprint of FII outflows - watch currency when flow data lags.
Panic days price far-OTM options richly: premium selling is the disciplined seller's response, sized for tail risk.

summary: Snap-back continues ('beach horse U-turn'): Friday's ~700-point fall mostly recovered; Bank Nifty weak early (-700) then last-half-hour Nifty +150/Bank +300 on institutional buying. 15,000CE and 14,800 straddle OI set up a squeeze above ~15,050-60; expects to reclaim the 15,100 February-expiry close. SGX gave -150 while pre-open was +100 - confused signals.
lessons: Max-OI walls are fuel: forced unwinding above the strike accelerates the move (positions drive price, not news).
'Amateurs open the market, professionals close it' - judge the day by the last half hour.

summary: Gap-down on Powell rate comments; SGX -300. FII -2,000cr AND DII -1,200cr - 'both big people beating the common man'. Strong US jobs (+379K vs 180K expected) initially sold off: 'very good news is bad news' via rate expectations. Bank Nifty broke 35,000 → short covering +400-500. 15,000 straddle 735→700; 14,000 put OI intact - support holds.
lessons: Good economic news can sell risk assets when it pulls forward rate-hike expectations - read data through the policy lens.
When FIIs and DIIs sell together, retail is the counterparty: expect outsized downside days.

summary: Whipsaw recap: Feb-expiry 15,100 → sub-14,500 in one session → 15,300 rebound → two gap-down days. Strong US payrolls (Dow +600 late); China Jan–Feb exports +60.6%/imports +22.2% beat. FII −₹2,000 cr/DII −₹1,000 cr; FIIs bought ₹13,000 cr options (2/3 puts). 15,000 CE +1.5M OI = squeeze fuel. SEBI margin rules thinning sellers. Range 14,500–15,500.
lessons: Max-OI signals fail in high-volatility regimes — heavy call writing into strength becomes upside fuel.
Post-SEBI-margin-rules scarcity of sellers keeps far-OTM premiums artificially rich — a structural edge for sellers.

summary: Expiry-week volatility (holiday shifted expiry to Wednesday): 200-up/200-down/200-up in Nifty; only private banks, financials, IT green. Surprise: FII +2,800cr AND DII +1,250cr - both buying. India VIX -9%. Thesis: five months of +50% showed first-half rallies and late-series chop; March sat exactly at 15,100 after 8 sessions; FIIs positioned light/short → upside squeeze risk; 14,000PE OI rising while price fell 100→35.
lessons: Light institutional positioning is upside fuel: crowded shorts get squeezed into expiry.
'I am a stupid guy - that is why I am an option seller': non-directional selling wins by not needing to be right.

summary: Peak margin (~15% on index futures vs ~5% international norm) ended broker intraday limits, forcing idle buffer cash and smaller positions. Fewer sellers meant richer premiums and a structurally higher India VIX. Proposes income thresholds or proficiency exams instead; cobra-effect parables for regulators.
lessons: Peak margin removed broker-funded intraday limits, so hedging legs need pre-funded buffer cash.
Fewer option sellers plus same buyers = higher premiums = structurally higher India VIX after the rules.
Margin hikes penalize the knowledgeable alongside the naive; access filters (income, exams) target risk directly.
Regulators risk the cobra effect: good intentions breeding the opposite outcome.

quotes: Regulators set out to catch snakes and ended up breeding them.

summary: Recorded on holiday in the hills: Friday 12 Mar saw a 250-pt gap-up fail at ~1:30pm institutional selling — Nifty −500 from high (~14,950 low), Bank Nifty −1,000; closed ~15,000 = Feb-expiry close. Whipsaw month: 15,000 straddle ₹800→₹600 (₹200). FII <₹1,000 cr. Upside cap 15,500. Range 14,500–15,500.
lessons: In a whipsaw month, the short straddle earns without predicting — volatility premium is the trade.
Gap-ups near all-time highs into thin liquidity are fade candidates; 1:30pm is the institutional session's turn.

summary: Son-crying joke mirrors the market selling on assumed FII outflows that data doesn't show. Breadth diverged: mid/small caps, IT, pharma, FMCG up while IndusInd, HDFC Bank, ICICI sat in the bottom five - private-bank-specific selling. Doji close = 'calm before storm'; VIX back above 20. OI: 15,000 heavy = resistance; 14,700 straddle ~250 (range 14,500-15,000); Bank Nifty OI at 34,000/34,500/35,000. Expiry call: above 15K or below 14.5K.
lessons: Markets often front-run feared flows: price falls on the assumption of FII selling before any actual selling.
Doji after a volatile month flags an imminent decisive move - plan both branches (expiry >15K or <14.5K).

summary: Data-proven lesson: with Nifty down 500+ points, VIX collapsing 65 to ~55 made even deep puts lose value - buyers lost despite right direction. Prescribes buy+sell ratio structures instead of naked longs in falling VIX.
lessons: In a falling-VIX environment, correct directional views still lose money - vega swamps delta for option buyers.
Weekly, monthly and far-month puts ALL fell or stagnated during a 500-point drop - the effect is structural, not decay noise.
Do not buy naked options when VIX is falling; run structures that own a short premium leg.
Television-expert option-buying advice during high VIX is exactly the trap to avoid.

strategies.best_regime: Falling VIX with a directional view; benefits from vega collapse on the short legs

summary: Post-breakout consolidation 8,800-9,350; RBI announcement day saw Bank Nifty crash then surge (private bank index +7%, Axis +15%); PCR 0.88-0.9 = oversold despite 20% rally; 9,000-10,000 OI range; pent-up auto demand thesis.
lessons: Put-call ratio ~0.9 after a 20% rally means still oversold - room for short covering, not top.
The more times a level (38.2% Fib ~9,300) is tested, the higher the odds of breakout.

Buying 1 and selling 2 at a higher strike creates a near-zero-cost position with capped downside
Far-out risk (above 410) is acceptable only when the stock has shown no ability to get there

summary: Firefighting walkthrough on an ICICI Bank call-ratio position after a results miss: original 350/380 call spread risked ~Rs 0.50/share; by selling 400CE at 3.65 once the stock weakened, the position flipped to net credit and profit. Advises small traders to stick to indices.
lessons: When a thesis breaks, sell a further OTM option to convert the position into a net credit instead of accepting the planned loss.
Stock options move violently; small-capital traders should stick to indices.
Announce the risk of a trade before the event, then adjust mechanically after - not emotionally.

strategies.name: OTM credit-sale adjustment on a losing ratio
strategies.construction: Existing: long 350CE, short 2x 380CE (max loss ~0.50/share ~ Rs 800/lot). Adjustment: sell 1x 400CE at ~3.65
strategies.numbers: Pre-adjustment loss ~Rs 3,000; post-adjustment profit ~Rs 2,000 per lot
strategies.best_regime: After a results miss confirms the directional view is dead
strategies.adjustments: Collected credit exceeds the defined max loss; no further action needed unless stock reverses hard
strategies.risks: New short call adds upside risk; acceptable because view is now neutral-bearish

summary: Builds a limited-risk call ratio on the post-COVID rally: buy 1x 10,500 Aug CE @360, sell 3x 11,000 Aug CE, buy 2x 11,500 Aug CE; net credit ~1,900; margin ~63,000 effective; max profit ~37,000 at Nifty 11,000; breakeven 11,253; max loss ~37,000 above 11,500; anchored on 200-DMA + 50% Fibonacci resistance.
lessons: Turn a 'resistance holds' view into a credit ratio spread; add far calls to cap the unlimited-risk tail.
Net-credit gating: if the structure is a debit in the near expiry, step out to the far month where it pays you.
Margin-benefit rules let 2-3 lakh accounts run defined-risk ratio structures.

strategies.name: Limited-risk call ratio spread (1:3:2)
strategies.construction: Buy 1x 10,500 CE (Aug), sell 3x 11,000 CE (Aug), buy 2x 11,500 CE (Aug)
strategies.numbers: Net credit ~Rs 1,900; margin ~Rs 65,000 (Rs 63,000 effective); max profit ~Rs 37,000 at Nifty 11,000; upper breakeven 11,253; max loss ~Rs 37,000 above 11,500
strategies.best_regime: After a sharp rally, into strong resistance (200-DMA + 50% retracement of 12,400->7,500)

summary: Market recap (HDFC Bank deposit-growth gap-up, Reliance+HDFC Bank over half the Nifty rally, FIIs and DIIs both net buyers) plus a clean explainer: extraordinary dividends (>5% of market value) trigger option strike adjustments on ex-date - ITC's 10-rupee dividend reset strikes; brokers cannot change strikes at will. Dividend-capture via cash buy + futures short pocketed ~5% in days.
lessons: When a dividend exceeds 5% of market value, exchanges adjust option strikes (and premiums) on ex-date - the broker did not change anything; check corporate actions before trading stock options.
Ex-dividend drops create a short-lived arbitrage: buy cash, short futures, collect the dividend, square both at convergence.
Market leadership can flip intraday (HDFC Bank morning, Reliance afternoon) - concentration of two names driving >50% of an index rally is a fragility signal.

strategies.name: Dividend capture via cash-futures arbitrage
strategies.construction: Buy stock in cash market before ex-date; short equal futures; collect dividend; square both legs post ex-date
strategies.numbers: ITC dividend >10 rupees on a ~200 rupee stock; ~5% return in days as stated
strategies.best_regime: Extraordinary dividends (>5% of market value) where futures still price the gross dividend
strategies.adjustments: Square up after ex-date convergence
strategies.risks: Futures may already price the dividend; margin on short futures; execution costs

quotes: whenever a company declares a dividend more than 5% of the market value... option prices will be adjusted

summary: Live pre-results ITC structure: buy 2 lots 197.5CE at 6.55, sell 4 lots 205CE at 3.50, plus sell 2 lots 185PE at 1.05 as a willing-delivery floor; ~Rs 2.3-2.5L margin, ~Rs 50k max profit near 205, upper breakeven ~214; downside plan is taking delivery on a 5%+ dividend yield.
lessons: Pre-earnings ratio spreads monetize a range view: profit concentrates at the sold strike, risk only beyond the far breakeven.
Sell puts only at prices you are happy to take delivery - a 5%+ dividend yield makes the floor rational.
Broker margin tools can misreport exotic strikes; cross-check with a second calculator before sizing.
State risk and reward up front; never pass risk blame to others after following someone's trade.

strategies.name: ITC pre-earnings call ratio with put floor
strategies.construction: Buy 2 lots 197.5CE @6.55; sell 4 lots 205CE @3.50; sell 2 lots 185PE @1.05 (July 2020 expiry)
strategies.numbers: Max profit ~Rs 50,000 near 205; loss begins beyond 212.5 (upper breakeven ~214 after put leg); margin ~Rs 2.31-2.5 lakh (Opstra showed 41k - wrong); underlying 3-month high 208
strategies.best_regime: Mildly bullish stock in a range into results, with high dividend yield cushioning the downside
strategies.adjustments: Take delivery below 185 (long-term buy thesis); adjust/firefight on a breakout above 212.5
strategies.risks: Gap above the 3:2 short-call ratio (225+) after results; assignment/obligation on short leg

quotes: When the reward comes you do not pass it on to others; when the risk comes, do not pass the blame on others.

summary: Pair trading as a market-neutral structure: long one instrument, short another (often same sector, e.g., long HDFC/ICICI vs short SBI/BoB; long Maruti vs short Tata Motors). COVID example: Maruti -33% while Tata Motors -85% made the pair hugely profitable. Live demonstration with Nifty long / Bank Nifty short across one week, two weeks and one month (Aug 2020) showing positive net P&L in all three windows as Nifty outperformed (10,200 -> ~11,300 while Bank Nifty crawled 21,500 -> 21,800).
lessons: Pair trading isolates relative strength: you profit from the spread between two instruments, not from market direction - gaps and crashes largely cancel.
Classic pairs: private banks long vs PSU banks short; quality autos long vs weak autos short; index long vs lagging index short.
Spread math dominates: when Nifty rose ~1,100 points while Bank Nifty rose ~300, the long-Nifty/short-BankNifty pair collected the differential on both legs.
Divergent beta is the edge and the risk: in a crash the 'strong' leg can fall just as hard - pairs are hedged, not riskless ('fail proof' is sales talk).

strategies.name: Nifty long / Bank Nifty short pair
strategies.construction: Long 1 lot Nifty futures + short 1 lot Bank Nifty futures (25 lot size), rebalanced views weekly
strategies.numbers: One-week window: ~4,725 loss on Nifty leg vs ~12,775 profit on Bank Nifty leg; two-week window: net ~12,000+ profit; one-month window positive
strategies.best_regime: Index divergence phases - Bank Nifty underperforming Nifty for weeks
strategies.adjustments: Re-evaluate pair weekly; exit when the spread normalizes
strategies.risks: Correlation breakdown in crashes; both legs can lose if sized wrong; margin on two futures legs

quotes: Pair trading means going long in one stock and going short in another - the differential profit is your profit.

summary: Classifies derivatives participants into arbitrageurs, hedgers, speculators; teaches arbitrage via the tomato two-price example and the old inter-exchange (BSE-Madras) trade; personal 1995 story: borrowing at 3% in Singapore to park in 20% NRNR deposits, currency risk hedged with a forward at ~2%/yr cost, netting ~15% riskless.
lessons: Arbitrage = buy where cheap, sell where dear, simultaneously; technology and algos have closed the old manual inter-exchange gaps
Borrow low in one currency, deposit high in another, and hedge the currency leg with a forward - the residual is near-riskless carry
Hedging a carry trade costs something (here ~2%/yr); the true arbitrage is the spread minus the hedge cost
Speculators take directional risk and provide the liquidity that hedgers and arbitrageurs need

strategies.name: Covered interest carry trade (1995 example)
strategies.construction: Borrow SGD at 3%, place INR NRNR deposit at 20%, hedge FX with a 3-year forward costing ~2%/yr
strategies.numbers: gross spread 17%; net ~15% riskless; 10 lakh -> ~17.5 lakh over 3 years
strategies.best_regime: large interest-rate differentials with hedged currency risk
strategies.adjustments: roll forward hedge; watch repatriation rules
strategies.risks: counterparty/country risk; hedge cost creep

quotes: Buy where it is cheap, sell where it is dear, at the same time - the difference is your profit, with no risk

summary: Mission Options E09: classifies strikes as ITM/ATM/OTM relative to spot with NSE chain color-coding (white = OTM, yellow = ITM for calls); compares cost, probability and payoff of 12,500CE (600), 13,000CE (275) and 13,500CE (75) with expiry scenarios at 13,400/13,000/12,500; concludes ITM is his preferred choice for higher win probability.
lessons: ITM options cost more but have the highest win probability; OTM options are cheap but rarely win - retail's lottery-ticket bias is buying far OTM.
ATM sits between: moderate premium, moderate probability.
Strike selection is a probability-reward trade-off: same view, three very different payoff distributions (worked scenarios at 13,400/13,000/12,500).
NSE chain color-codes calls: white = OTM, yellow = ITM (reversed for puts).

strategies.name: Strike-selection framework (ITM vs ATM vs OTM)
strategies.construction: Same directional view expressed via 12,500CE / 13,000CE / 13,500CE with spot ~13,000
strategies.best_regime: ITM for high-probability moderate moves; OTM only for large fast moves
strategies.adjustments: exit anytime; premium decays
strategies.risks: OTM total loss most probable; ITM larger absolute rupee loss

quotes: In the money options are high risk and high reward and out of the money options are low risk and low reward.

summary: Live budget-day trade log: sold 10x 14,700CE @ Rs 8, sold 10x 13,500PE @ ~Rs 137, bought 5x 13,800PE @ ~Rs 245 (plus a 12,500PE @ Rs 10 elsewhere) - breakeven 13,155, upside risk 14,720, max P/L ~Rs 12,000, 81% PoP. Explains far-OTM options moving opposite to the market in high volatility; silver 'next GameStop' squeeze attempt; markets rallying on short covering.
lessons: In violent markets, far-OTM options can move opposite to the index because traders buy them to cut margin - premium behavior beats price intuition.
After a global selloff, any good news triggers violent short covering - position for the squeeze, not the narrative.
Small-net-credit ratio structures can carry 81% probability with a few-thousand-rupee payoff - size for the risk, not the reward.
When everything hinges on one event, that event is the only variable worth tracking (budget, budget, budget).

strategies.name: Budget-day ratio structure (live)
strategies.construction: sold 10x 14,700CE @8; sold 10x 13,500PE @137; bought 5x 13,800PE @avg 245
strategies.numbers: downside breakeven 13,155; upside risk 14,720; max P/L ~Rs 12,000; PoP 81%; separate 12,500PE sold @10
strategies.best_regime: range-bound event day with bullish tilt
strategies.adjustments: further adjustments planned if 13,500 close is missed
strategies.risks: loss beyond 13,155 downside / 14,720 upside

quotes: In case a tiger chases us... all I have to do is run faster than you.

summary: Friday 26 Feb crash: Nifty −700+ intraday, Bank Nifty −2,000+; FII net −₹8,300 cr despite ~₹5,000 cr MSCI rebalancing inflows (gross >₹13,000 cr, possibly record). VIX ~30. GDP +0.4% beat-ish; J&J vaccine + House-passed $1.9tn stimulus. His put-ratio (buy 14,600 PE / sell 2× 14,000 PE). 50-DMA 14,400–450 bottom zone.
lessons: After a big crash the market needs hospital-rest before recovery — don't expect instant V-bounces.
OI is a guideline, not gospel — he faded the 14,000 PE support signal with a put ratio because his real risk line was 13,400.
High-VIX regimes are the option writer's harvest: far strikes still pay 4–5% a month.

summary: NSDL 'freezing' 3 FPI accounts holding ~Rs45,000cr Adani exposure triggered collateral-damage selling; Nifty fell 200+ then recovered to all-time-high close; Bank Nifty stayed weak; put writing in panic read as bullish; advance-tax disclosure.
lessons: Collateral damage: leveraged longs in crashing stocks are forced to sell unrelated holdings, spreading the fall.
Put writing continuing through a panic day signals seller conviction that downside is limited.
Retail should prefer indices over 'hot' single-stock stories; one gap-down can be 10-20%.

summary: Knee-jerk + expiry-day hangover explained; gap-down was fully recovered then sold from 1pm, final-hour covering; FII long cooled to 70%; IT dream run (Infosys >1500, near peak) - plans to sell Infosys 1600CE and a 1500/1580 call ratio.
lessons: FII long% band framework: 50-75% comfortable; >80% invites shakeouts; <50% fuels rallies.
When markets are bad IT does well (defensive + rupee), when markets are good money rotates out of IT.
Write calls against a parabolic stock only with position plan - Infosys near 'peak' is his read, not a law.

summary: Slightly bearish read: RIL broke 2,100 (-6-7% from recent high), 16,000 resistance firm; his 16,000/16,100/16,200 call sales in profit; put ratio deployed (buy 16,000PE, sell 2x 15,500PE; lower breakeven 15,000); FII long 82->80->78 drift; Friday jobs data + auto sales as triggers.
lessons: Put ratio (buy near put, sell 2x farther put) monetizes a mild bearish view with a wide profit zone and defined risk.
Track FII long% drift as a slow-burn regime indicator, not a day-trade signal.
Label your stance honestly ('slightly bearish, not ultra') - sizing follows the adjective.

summary: US CPI at 13-year high caused only mild profit booking; pendulum around equilibrium 15,750 rewards straddle/strangle sellers; OI anchors 15,700PE / 16,000CE; his Infosys call ratio spread: bought 1x1,540CE, sold 2x (1,580+1,600)CE at near-zero net cost - wins if flat/down, capped risk; Zomato IPO opens; BSE/CDSL surge = growing participation.
lessons: Call ratio spread (buy 1 near strike, sell 2 above) is a near-zero-cost mildly bullish structure with defined upside risk.
Range markets with a stable pivot reward systematic premium selling.

summary: The 2013 taper-tantrum lesson - low VIX strangles blew up 1 crore in a day - becomes the low-VIX rule: always mix buys with sells. Demonstrates an ITM far-month put calendar with NSE data and back-office proof (~10% in 3 weeks).
lessons: India VIX at multi-year lows is the most dangerous regime for pure option sellers - one VIX spike erases months of theta.
In low VIX, always pair buys with sells so a volatility spike cushions both legs.
Sell the in-the-money strike and hedge in a far month, not the adjacent month, when running put calendars.
A calendar's max loss is bounded by the debit structure even in a crash - that is the point of the hedge.

strategies.name: ITM put calendar (low-VIX regime)
strategies.construction: sell current-month ITM put (16,000PE July), buy same strike far-month put (16,000PE December) as the hedge

strategies.adjustments: exit early if VIX regime turns; keep partial hedge ratio honest (he ran 1,250 short vs 750 long)

quotes: Stock market is where people with money meet people with experience; after some time the experienced become the moneyed and the moneyed become the experienced.

summary: HDFC Bank results disappointment spreads to banks; Nifty -0.76%, Bank Nifty -1.89%; four financial stocks caused over half the fall; futures broke 15,600, ~380 points off Friday high; shorts built ahead of Reliance/ICICI results.
lessons: Bull-market corrections are fast and furious
Index-heavyweight results can flip market character within days

lessons: Breadth divergence: a handful of heavyweights can mask a bear market underneath a record index.
Event anticipation (Jackson Hole) is the real driver near record highs, not the record itself.

summary: Explains freak trades via NSE officials' own webinar material: futures circuit ladder 10%→20%→30% takes minutes to revise; options daily price ranges get widened reactively (50→80→300→1,920), so crowd stop-loss-market orders (9:20 straddle bots) fill at absurd prices - a Rs 400 stop executed at Rs 1,900, legal within the DPR. NSE banned SL-M orders from Sep 27, 2021. Core message: use SL-limit with a spread, take responsibility.
lessons: Stop-loss-market orders are structurally dangerous near crowded strikes: when everyone's trigger fires at once, your fill lands wherever liquidity is - within the day's legal price band.
Exchange circuit limits revise upward only after being hit; the gap between 'hit' and 'revised' is where freak fills happen.
Use SL-limit with a trigger-to-limit spread (even Rs 50-100 wide); you cap your worst fill without relying on the exchange.
Never outsource blame: if your counterpart acted within exchange limits, the loss is a tuition fee - take responsibility and change your order type.
quotes: You cannot change the world, but you can change yourself.

summary: Reviews an October 2021 Reliance earnings trade: 1-5-4 call butterfly (buy 2600CE, sell 5x2800CE, buy 4x3000CE) placed before Q2 results on an ATH-anchor view; exited next morning for profit instead of holding to expiry. Teaches butterfly mechanics and trade management.
lessons: In a butterfly, buys and sells must balance (1-5-4) — only then is risk limited and margin benefits apply.
Anchor strategy legs to the stock's all-time high: profit zone below the ATH, limited loss above it.
A strategy need not be held to expiry — exit into post-event strength or adjust; firefighting beats stubbornness.
Butterflies cap downside loss if the stock crashes, but upside loss beyond the upper strike is real money — hedge or manage it.

strategies.name: Call ratio butterfly (1-5-4) on Reliance before results
strategies.construction: Buy 1 lot 2600CE @ ~₹80; sell 5 lots 2800CE @ ~₹18-19; buy 4 lots 3000CE @ ~₹4-4.5 (equalized buys/sells for limited risk + margin benefit)

strategies.risks: Upside loss beyond upper strike (butterfly cap not free); time decay if event fizzes

summary: FII net buyers after 10 days; long Diwali weekend plus weekly expiry plus SBI results = violent trade; 18,000 call OI is 3x the 17,800 put OI; shares his live Reliance call-ratio (buy 2500 CE, sell 2x 2600 CE, near-zero downside, max profit at 2600); Sun TV +20% on Rajinikanth film release.
lessons: A call ratio funded by equal premium has no downside cost - structure matters more than view
Round-strike call OI triple the put OI means upside is the crowded, dangerous side

summary: Muhurat-session live trade walkthrough: Fed taper (Nov 3, 2021) passed without a crash — 'markets don't crash twice for the same reason'. Shows a smallcase diversified SIP (60% index ETFs, 10% gold as crash hedge, 30% debt/REITs) and a Dec-2022 no-loss-on-downside call-ratio-plus-cash-secured-put combo.
lessons: Markets don't crash twice for the same reason: first time is a surprise, second is experience (2013 taper −20% vs 2021 taper +green).
Central banks now sugar-coat tightening: pair every negative with a positive, and taper talk precedes taper by months.
A crash portfolio: ~60% index ETFs, ~10% gold (crisis hedge — gold rose in 2008 and 2020), ~30% debt/REITs you can liquidate to buy the dip.
Combine a call ratio (buy 1, sell 2 far) with a cash-secured put: no downside loss in a wide band, uncapped-ish profit in the middle.

strategies.numbers: Entered ~Nov 2021 with Nifty ~18,000; premiums ~350/1600/800; breakevens ~14,500 and ~22,700; margin ~₹1.5 lakh; target return 20-25% on margin

strategies.best_regime: After a sharp fall when recovery odds are good

quotes: Markets don't crash twice for the same reason — the first time is a surprise, the second time it is experience.
Drop a ball from the tenth floor and the rebound is huge — that is why 2008 and 2020 were followed by 100% years.

summary: Stable until 3pm basket sell: Nifty -70, Bank Nifty -200 in minutes; FII sold 975cr vs DII buy 1,007cr; milestone: Oct+Nov+Dec FII selling crossed Rs1 lakh crore - described as first time outside crises; Bajaj Auto EV announcement triggered auto short-covering; expiry-day call ratio executed (buy 2× 17,200 CE, sell 5× 17,300 CE).
lessons: Self-financed expiry-day structures (ratio spreads) monetize expected pinning without net premium outlay.
Late-session index-heavy basket orders are an institutional signature, not retail panic.

summary: Apple crossed $3 trillion market cap (history retold); US bank index +3%; SGX flat after 2-day, 1,500-pt rally; flat-open trend risk; DII profit-booking expected; FII added index futures longs; put:call ~1.5 weekly; FII long 70%; Bank Nifty breakout on FII favorites; TCS value spot (4,000→3,500→3,800); Infosys & TCS results Jan 12.
lessons: Put-call ratios near 1.5 in weekly options mark confident (crowded) bullish positioning - a contrarian watch-point.
Post-rally, high futures premiums are the market's own warning of near-term normalization.

summary: Pre-earnings TCS structure built live: a 1:3 call ratio (buy 3800C, sell three 4000C) with the extra credit spent on two OTM calls to cap risk, plus a 3700/3500 put spread for margin - breakevens 3678/4122, max profit 36,000, max loss 53,000 on ~1.5 lakh margin; sells the buyback-driven IV spike.
lessons: Sell event-inflated IV rather than buy it: the buyback announcement spiked premiums, and that spike was the trade.
Ratio spreads monetize a bounded directional view - long the move, short the overshoot, credit-funded wings for limited risk.
Hedged legs slash margin: a multi-lot structure ran on ~1.5 lakh because every short had a long against it.

summary: Follow-up to the Hindalco physical-settlement case where an option buyer lost 13 lakh on a 1 lakh premium: explains buyer margins escalating through expiry week, broker liability to the exchange regardless of client default, offsetting delivery for spreads/covered calls, removal of the do-not-exercise facility, and four escalating solutions.
lessons: Option buyers pay only premium until expiry week; brokers then escalate buyer margin 20-40-60-80-100% by Thursday or square off.
The exchange collects losses from the broker even if the client defaults; recovery is a broker-client legal matter.
Spread and covered-call legs mutually offset physical delivery only when both legs finish in the money.
The do-not-exercise facility (ATM plus 3 strikes) was removed in November 2021 - close-to-the-money holders can no longer abandon intrinsic value.
quotes: Exchange will deduct the money from the broker's account whether the client pays or not.

summary: Crypto options status update: a 2,000 USDT free-capital book grew to about 7,535 USDT (~350%) in 2-3 months. Demonstrates funding transfer via XRP, then builds an Ethereum June structure: buy 1x 3000 call, sell 3x 5000 calls, sell 2x 2000 puts, with breakevens near 1,850 and 6,160 and a martingale roll-up plan above 5,000.
lessons: High-risk strategies are acceptable only with tiny, non-essential capital - max loss is capped at the stake.
Never allocate more than about 10% of capital to crypto; keep accessible reserves to top up after crashes.
Far out-of-the-money strikes carry double demand (hedgers plus margin-conscious sellers), so selling them captures richer premium.
Option buyers should ride momentum and exit; sellers hold to expiry but must plan adjustments.

strategies.name: Ethereum call ratio financed by short puts (long-term)
