summary: Budget-day trade log (recorded then shown live): with US VIX under 25 and Nifty already corrected from 18,600 to 17,300, sold a Nifty put ladder (weekly 17,000-16,600; monthly 16,500-16,000), a Bank Nifty put ladder (36,500-36,000), put ratios (buy 17,600PE/sell 2x 17,300PE; buy 39,000PE/sell 2x 38,000PE), and 30%-stop-loss short straddles (BN 38,600; Nifty 17,500). Intraday P&L ~3.4 lakh, net ~27 lakh.
lessons: Enter binary events with low expectations after a correction - downside surprise is then limited.
US VIX below 25 is a permission slip for premium selling into the event.
Sell far out-of-the-money puts where hedgers and margin-traders create double demand.
Straddle stop-loss rule: 30% of one side's premium; if one side is stopped, move the other side's stop to cost - max loss equals one side's 30%.

strategies.construction: Weekly puts 17,000-16,600 (Nifty); monthly 16,500-16,000; Bank Nifty 36,500-36,000 (all sold)

summary: Crypto-crash aftermath and rebuild: a 7,500 USDT book fell to 4,500, was topped up to ~21,000, and still shows ~5,000 profit. ETH positions net -$110 despite the 20-25% crash. Wide-breakeven combos absorb crypto violence: profit across 15,000-60,000 BTC despite 20-25% underlying crashes.
What-if simulation (time decay plus IV shift) is due diligence before executing any multi-leg structure.

summary: March-deadline tax planning explainer. ELSS under 80C (Rs.1.5 lakh): five mistakes - last-week lump-sum timing risk (prefer monthly SIP of ~12,500), yearly fund-hopping, redeeming right after the 3-year lock-in (hold 8-10 years for 12-15% vs FD 8-9%), mismatching fund market-cap style to risk profile, and chasing last year's winner instead of 5-10-year record vs benchmark. NPS: extra Rs.50,000 under 80CCD(1B); at retirement 60% withdrawable (tax-free), 40% must buy annuity; equity/debt mix chosen by age and risk.
lessons: Spread tax investments through the year - last-week lump sums carry pure timing risk.
One well-chosen fund beats a shelf of annual switches; monitor less, hold longer.
A 3-year lock-in is a minimum, not a horizon: mutual funds reward 8-10-year holds.
Choose ELSS market-cap style by risk profile; small caps pay in bulls and punish in bears.
quotes: We never study until one day before the exam - the same way we save tax only in the last week of March.

lessons: Gap-ups without news fade; gap-ups with genuine news sustain.
Futures-premium expansion signals short covering, not fresh longs.

summary: Earnings-week IT strategy ahead of TCS results (11-Apr) and Infosys (13-Apr). Context: TCS range 3,400-4,000 (Jan high on 4,000 buyback news; Ukraine-war gap to 3,400; pre-result dip to 3,650); Accenture's strong print is a read-through. Executed structure: buy 1x 3,600 CE, sell 3x 3,800 CE, buy 2x 4,000 CE, sell 2x 3,400 PE, buy 2x 3,200 PE - a ratio spread with both wings capped; margin cut from ~Rs.2 lakh to ~Rs.1.22 lakh, max profit ~Rs.30,000 near a 3,800 close, POP ~68%, breakevens 3,400-3,900, max loss ~Rs.59,000.
lessons: Same-business read-throughs work: Accenture's results telegraph Indian IT results ('same people, same mindset').
A call ratio is safe only with a capped upside wing - and capping also slashes margin.
Wing both sides around the earnings range: sold 3,400 PE anchored on the 3,400 war-low support.
Strategy strikes should come from the stock's own range map (buyback level, war gap, consolidation), not hope.

Divide capital into 10-15 parallel strategies so rescue capital always exists without closing winners.
Return-on-investment framing misleads for collateral-based sellers; absolute profit and capital-at-risk both matter.

Higher interest rates are not inherently bad for banks or equities (2003-2007 rising rates with rising markets).

High dividend yield is not a floor (Vedanta 19% yield still fell 15%) - but deeply out-of-favor high-yielders are where he prefers to bottom-fish.

lessons: Falling on low volume = absence of panic selling; rising on low volume = absence of conviction - read volume with price.
Option-writing hedges (100-point spreads) cap max loss at a known quantity - define risk before the trade, not after.
A 25-30% correction in a quality large-cap (TCS) has historically been a good entry - but this time may differ; verify, don't assume.

summary: US Q1 GDP revised to -1.6% (vs -1.5% expected) yet US ignored it - already priced after a 1,000-point Dow drop. Reliance-Jio news drove India's recovery; TCS making violent two-way moves; Nifty futures ~20-30 point discount into expiry hinting bearish bias. Stability only when the Fed slows to 25bp hikes (Sept/Oct at the earliest). His Reliance 2,500CE/2,600CE spread into expiry.
lessons: Once a market has absorbed a shock (1,000-point Dow drop), a slightly worse headline loses its power - sequencing of news matters more than the news.
Futures discount/premium shifts into expiry are a positioning tell: persistent discount hints at bearish bias in the resolution.

lessons: A 12% index-weight stock falling 8% is a mechanical ~1% index hit: always know your index's heavyweight concentration risk.
Futures calendar-spread discount collapsing to premium is a classic short-covering tell - more reliable than opinion.

summary: India underperformed ahead of US CPI: Bank Nifty fell ~250-300 in the final 45 minutes; TCS slid toward 3,000 (from 4,000; buyback was at 4,500); Infosys the top drag. FII selling resumed (-1,565 cr), futures shorts back above 80%. lessons: Before a binary macro event, cut to long-horizon structures with IV-collapse exit plans - the event trade is premium behavior, not direction.
A 1:3 put ratio with breakeven 1,800 points below spot is a defined-risk way to hold a long-horizon hedge through an event.

Position MTM swings of lakhs are normal for large December-options books.

Markets rally on 'bad' news when it is expected: 9.1% CPI, a 75bp hike and negative GDP all produced up-days in late July 2022.

Fund a ratio trade's extra cost by selling OTM puts rather than adding cash.

strategies.construction: Buy 2,900 calls (approx 4 lots @ ~40); sell ~8 lots @ ~37; sell 6 lots of ~2,500 strikes @ ~25; buy 2 lots of higher call as tail hedge (transcript garbled on exact strikes)
strategies.numbers: Net credit ~225 points collected vs ~179 spent; stated 70% probability; max profit ~3 lakh plus 45,000; breakevens below 2,500 and above 3,000; margin ~15 lakh; at recording -7,300 open

strategies.adjustments: If stock gaps against view, treat as firefighting case; rely on post-results IV collapse
strategies.risks: Stock can fall 10% in one session on results; garbled legs in transcript - strikes need re-verification before use

summary: Post-mortem of a wrong pre-results view on IndusInd Bank: bought 8,600 calls 2 lots at 33, sold 6 lots at 11 (1:3 ratio), sold far-OTM 800 puts at 2.8 to convert naked-call margin into hedged margin. Strong results gapped the stock up; the rescue used a put-selling ladder (880 through 950) plus a costless upside collar (bought 950 calls for 2 lakh funded by selling 1,000 calls); exited above 1,000 with ~95,000 profit on ~30 lakh churned margin (~3%).
lessons: Buying the far leg in a 1:3 call ratio and selling puts converts both naked legs into hedged margin - pay almost nothing extra.
Stop the bleeding first, treat later: when a position is gapping against you, cap the tail before planning the recovery.
A costless collar (buy near call, sell far call for equal premium) caps disaster for zero cash.
The same margin block is reused repeatedly in a ladder - track churned margin, not just peak margin.

strategies.name: IndusInd 1:3 call ratio with put-funded margin hedge and ladder rescue
strategies.construction: Buy 2 lots 8600CE @33; sell 6 lots @11 (1:3); sell 800PE @2.8 for margin hedge; rescue: sell 880/900/910/920/940/950 puts progressively; at >950 buy 950CE (~30, funded by selling 1000CE); square off above 1,000
strategies.numbers: Breakeven ~920; net result +95,000 on ~30 lakh churned margin (~3%); one ladder step made +19,000
strategies.best_regime: Pre-earnings mildly bearish view that is proved wrong by a gap up
strategies.adjustments: Stop-bleed collar first; then profit ladder on put sales as stock climbs
strategies.risks: If stock reversed from 950 back to 850-900 the put ladder itself would need fresh firefighting; tail above strike funded only by collar

quotes: When a person meets with an accident, the first objective is to stop the bleeding, and only then the treatment starts.
For every put I sold I had to block about 6 lakh of margin - but the same margin gets released and reused.

summary: Builds a hedged carry trade: buy sovereign gold bonds at a ~10% discount to physical gold, pledge them as trading collateral (cash component), short MCX gold futures to remove price risk, and harvest contango roll profits (~31% on the margin deployed).
lessons: Cash-futures arbitrage is mostly dead in India - transaction costs and algo competition eat the spread.
SGB trades at a discount to physical gold and pays 2.5% interest: discount unwind plus interest gives ~4% pre-carry return.
Pledging SGB as collateral (counts as cash component) lets a trader stay invested AND trade on the limit.
Shorting MCX gold futures against SGB removes gold-price risk entirely; contango roll adds extra return each renewal.

strategies.name: SGB + short MCX gold futures hedged carry
strategies.construction: Buy SGB (e.g. 1kg equivalent ~50L); pledge as collateral; short 1kg MCX gold futures using ~5L of the limit; roll short at each expiry (contracts every 2 months)
strategies.numbers: SGB ~4,800/g vs physical ~5,300/g (~10% discount); GOI interest 2.5%/yr + ~1.5%/yr discount unwind = ~4%; roll spread ~130-150 per 10g per month ~ 1.56L/yr on 5L margin = ~31% ROI; optional overlay: sell 50,000 put @150 (10g) for extra ~3,000/month
strategies.best_regime: When SGB trades at a wide discount and MCX gold is in contango; for F&O traders with collateral requirement
strategies.adjustments: Roll the short future to the next series each expiry; optionally add short put when already short future (no extra margin)
strategies.risks: Roll spread can shrink to near zero; margin calls if gold spikes sharply (temporary MTM); SGB liquidity is limited; interest is taxable at slab rate

quotes: You are long in gold sovereign bond, short in future - one long and one short, you carry zero risk.

summary: Opened below SGX indication and free-fell: no recovery all day; Bank Nifty -1,400 in two sessions; Europe (Germany-led) killed the 12:30 bounce; VWAP sellers added fuel; both FII (-450cr) and DII (-85cr) sold - no support; his defensive bear put spread 17,500/17,400 (pay 60, max 100).
lessons: When both FIIs and DIIs sell, no institution absorbs the fall - retail is the only bid, and rallies get sold into
Technical VWAP sellers with stops 10-20 points above accelerate any decline that reaches VWAP - know where the machinery will sell

summary: Jackson Hole: Powell's 9-minute hawkish speech ('pain') sent Dow down ~1,100 intraday (1,500-pt swing), Nasdaq -5%+; ~$78B rich-list loss per Bloomberg. SGX -200 for Monday; speaker flips bullish-to-bearish; 18,000 seen as ceiling. Stock of week: Reliance pre-AGM bull call spread 2500/2600; AGM hopes: Jio/Retail IPOs, 5G plans, green energy; 15-30% one-year upside thesis.
lessons: Bad news ignored for months can suddenly matter - first over-reaction marks trend change.
Buy-the-dip works only until the tape says sell-on-rise; respect the switch.

summary: Hong Kong (-1.5%, one of only two global markets 30%+ off highs) drags SGX Nifty to ~17,510. Russia's gas halt to Europe is already priced - crude +1.5%. Financials strong vs non-financials weak. Teaches a live call calendar: long 17,500CE monthly, short 17,500CE weekly, harvesting faster near-term decay. Futures premium collapsed ~100 to ~15-20 points.
lessons: Calendar spread mechanics: same strike, buy far month, sell near month - the near leg's faster decay is the edge.
Futures premium is a froth gauge; its collapse warns that bullish conviction has drained.

summary: Muhurat session (Oct 24, 1 hr) closed ~17,700-17,750; SGX now ~17,800. Xi's third term crushing China/HK/Taiwan; Chinese ADRs -10-15% in US after -7-8% Friday. ICICI Bank spiked 5-6% in Muhurat's last minutes (speaker had sold 920 CE, rolled to 940, now vulnerable); Reliance flat on mediocre results. Watchlist: short Reliance/Kotak, long ICICI/Axis; pair-trade idea short Kotak vs long ICICI/Axis. Stock OIs collapsed - crowd expects a big move, direction unknown; December put premiums crashing / call premiums rising → upside hint. Sold 17,600 PE; Bank Nifty put ladder 41,000→40,000 in 20-lot tranches to spread firefighting risk. FIIs -154 cr, DIIs +80 cr (Muhurat). Expiry hopes ~17,800 vs last month 16,800.
lessons: Ladder put sales across strikes (20 lots each at 200-pt spacing) so any single firefight is 20% of the book - spread risk, not reward.
When stock OI collapses across the board, the market is paying for a move it cannot direction - wait for the reveal.

summary: India decoupled: Nifty +300 despite Nasdaq -8-9% on the Fed and jobs. Bank Nifty hit ATH then corrected; PSU banks outperformed (SBI ATH Friday after results 540 to 590). Bank of Baroda anecdote: worst-ever quarter (3,400 crore loss) followed by +25% next day on 'worst is over'. Call ratio 580/610 on SBI. Trending market - selling puts below 17,800, scared to sell calls. Metals strong despite weak results. Range 18,000-18,500; Thursday US CPI, ATH 18,600 possible Friday.
lessons: Results-day reaction is driven by positioning, not by the print itself.
In a trending market, sell puts rather than calls - and respect the regime change.

summary: Walks through a Dec-2023-expiry combo demoed at conferences: long 16,000CE (2,450), short 2x 20,000CE (700 each) and short 3x 13,000PE (~285-300) for net debit ~150; the short puts collapsed to ~60 and were squared off, then rolled to 15,000PE for ~2.75 lakh more - total ~3.4 lakh as Nifty rallied and VIX collapsed 20-21 to 12-13. Frames Buffett's LEAPS selling and Nov-Feb as the long-dated sweet spot.
lessons: Long-dated combos let trend plus falling IV compound; both tailwinds stacked in late 2022.
When a short leg collapses toward zero quickly, square it off and redeploy closer to the money (rolled 13,000PE to 15,000PE).
November-February is the best window to initiate long-dated option structures.
30-40% a year is a realistic long-dated target; the demo's bigger profit was an extraordinary VIX-collapse bonus.

strategies.name: Long-dated ratio combo (LEAPS-style)
strategies.construction: Buy 1 lot Dec-2023 16,000CE @2,450; sell 2 lots 20,000CE @700 each; sell 3 lots 13,000PE @~285-300
strategies.numbers: Net debit ~150; later short 13,000PE fell 285->60 (2 lots squared off), rolled to 15,000PE for ~2.75 lakh additional; running profit ~3.4 lakh; VIX 20-21 -> 12-13; benchmark expectation 30-40% p.a.
strategies.best_regime: Post-correction bullish setup with elevated IV in Nov-Feb; far expiries
strategies.adjustments: Book collapsed short legs early; roll short puts nearer as the index rallies
strategies.risks: Illiquidity in far strikes; a VIX spike instead of collapse would hurt; unlimited put-side loss if index crashes

quotes: Who is the largest option seller in the world? Warren Buffett... he always plays in LEAPS.
This profit is an extraordinary profit just because VIX crashed from 20-21 to 12-13.

summary: Long-term bullish combo revealed: 10 lots Nifty Dec-2022 futures long @17,200 hedged by next-Dec 17,000 put bought @1,410, premium funded by selling 1,500 qty 21,000 calls @~455. MTM +8L future, -5L put, +22K calls; rolls futures into Jan-Feb until Dec-2023.
lessons: A far-dated put can be fully funded by selling far-OTM calls, turning a leveraged long into a near-zero-premium protected bet.
Roll futures monthly; keep the hedge structure intact across series.
Nov-Feb is the prime window for long-term options positions.
Admit the hedge bleeds (put -5L vs future +8L) and offset it with short puts lower down rather than dismantling the structure.

strategies.name: Hedged long-term combo (funded protective put)
strategies.construction: Long 10 lots Nifty Dec futures @17,200; buy 500 qty next-Dec 17,000 put @1,410; sell 1,500 qty 21,000 calls @~455 x3 series to fund the put
strategies.numbers: Put cost ~7L funded by call premium ~7L; MTM: +8L futures, -5L put, +22K calls; net ~+5L
strategies.best_regime: Structurally bullish view with 12-18 month horizon; Nov-Feb entry window
strategies.adjustments: Roll futures at expiry; sold extra 15,000/16,000 puts to offset put-side bleed; adjust calls if market nears 21,000
strategies.risks: Market below 15,000 makes the extra short puts troublesome; bleed continues if market chops sideways

quotes: I have a right to be wrong.

summary: HCL Tech's mid-quarter guidance cut (−6%) dragged IT; Nifty −250 for week ex-banks −450 while Bank Nifty +450. Broke 18,500 Friday. Dec 12-16 packed: India CPI/IIP Mon, US CPI Tue, Fed Wed, quadruple witching Fri. Monthly range 18,000-19,000 intact.
lessons: When one heavyweight reports shock news off-cycle, the collateral damage spreads beyond that stock — reduce index exposure, not just the stock.
A fat futures premium over spot has reliably preceded corrections; it is a positioning warning, not a prediction.

summary: Rapid-fire Q&A: REIT collateral limits, cost of rolling Bank Nifty futures for a year (~100 pt/month premium), why stock lending & borrowing loses to futures shorting, margin-adequacy math for 2-lot Nifty short, trading-ban MWPL thresholds, Bharat Bond volatility, correction-vs-crash definitions after Tesla's 21% day and $1T US tech wipeout.
lessons: Rolling long futures costs ~5-6% a year in premium; long-term positions belong in cash, shorts earn the premium.
Stock lending & borrowing loses to futures shorting: no futures premium, borrowing cost, and full option margin on the hedge.
Market-wide position limit above 95% bans a stock; the ban persists until it falls below 80% - even on expiry day.
Margin money is calibrated to cover ~99% of moves: 2 short Nifty lots lose only ~35-40K in a 500-point gap against 1L+ margin.

strategies.name: Bank Nifty rollover analysis
strategies.construction: Long (or short) futures rolled monthly

strategies.best_regime: Long-term shorts benefit from rollover premium; long-term longs should buy cash instead
strategies.adjustments: Hedging is cheaper on futures than on cash positions
strategies.risks: Premium varies 40-200 pts monthly; longs underperform cash by the premium

quotes: The bloodbath will continue as long as there is blood.
Margin money will take care of 99% of the time - the problem comes only when Nifty falls more than 1,500 points.

summary: Calm firm day: SGX +120, closed +120; banks/NBFC led by HDFC twins; both FIIs (+114cr) and DIIs (+344cr) net buyers - rare; will Nifty hit 16,000; pre-result profit booking in run-up stocks (Infosys -50/60); his put calendar: sold July 16,000PE ~400, bought Dec 16,000PE (ITM, far-month) - both legs profitable, >10% return; 16,000 expected in July series.
lessons: ITM put calendar (sell near-month, buy far-month same strike) earns from direction and time with bounded risk.
Stocks that run into results see pre-result profit booking; beaten-down ones see short covering.

summary: Technicians extrapolating 2008 and 2020 (crash then +110-120% in 12-15 months) project Nifty 35,000 by end-2023 from the June 2022 low of ~15,200. The speaker argues 99.99% against it: 2008/2020 recoveries rode 0% rates and QE; 2022 has a hiking Fed and QT. Lesson: be a techno-fundamentalist. Includes an REC bonus-issue anecdote destroying a mean-reversion trade, and two December-2023 long-dated strategies shown at a Dubai conference.
lessons: Pattern-matching past crashes fails when the policy regime differs: 2008/2020 recoveries needed 0% rates + QE; 2022 had rising rates + QT.
Do not be a pure technician or pure fundamentalist - be a techno-fundamentalist; charts plus macro context.
Mean reversion breaks on corporate actions: REC's fall from 140 to 105 was a 1:3 bonus adjustment, not a correction - the retracement trade expired worthless.
Long-dated option combos can carry wide breakevens and produce windfall months, but 'you cannot make this kind of profit every time'.

If any technical analyst looks at the chart pattern of 2008 and 2020, he will assume 30,000-35,000. But there is a catch.

summary: Post-rally consolidation day before Holi holiday. Weekend: Amazon halts HQ-2 construction, Meta cuts VR headset prices - Nasdaq pause after +5% in two sessions. Week loaded: Powell speech, ADP, claims, jobs. Focus: Reliance windfall-tax cut, Tata Steel/PFC long build-up, Manappuram short covering + SBI MF stake. Rupee broke 82 (~81.75). His put calendar: sell weekly 18,000 PE, buy monthly 18,000 PE. VIX 12.18 multi-year low.
lessons: At very low VIX do not sell naked options - combine buying and selling (calendars/ratios)
Rupee strength plus DII/FII support is a tailwind trio for Indian equities

summary: Dow's 'sell in May' scoreboard: zero returns since April-end; hawkish Fed dot plot (two more hikes vs one expected) knocked Dow, crude, gold and crypto (worst, -5-6%). His Fed frame: hawkish when markets are strong, dovish when weak - 'the game of moderation'. China cutting rates; Asia decoupled and higher. New supply overhang: Bain Capital looking to sell ~$167M of Axis Bank (only ~1.5% stake, small discount). Suggests a long-dated calendar to a friend: sell current-month 20,000 PE, buy December 20,000 PE, roll monthly - a 20,000-target lottery ticket with capped downside, plus far-CE cover. Levels: expiry pin 18,700-18,900; Bank Nifty 43,500-44,500 for the month.
lessons: A long-dated put calendar on a round-number target converts a conviction view into capped-risk optionality
Markets gap-fade: huge gaps retrace; flat opens are where trends are born

summary: Builds a case for Nifty 20,000 in 3-4 months (heavyweight catch-up, rolling-return mean reversion, supertrend 21/53 trend-persistence) and demonstrates a deep-ITM put calendar as a low-margin bullish alternative to naked put selling, with roll costs as the defined monthly risk.
lessons: Two supertrend lines (20-day/5-day) proxy monthly and weekly trends; alignment defines regime.
Trends historically persisted 10-12 weeks; extensions beyond that signaled outsized continuation rallies (post-COVID, post-inflation).
A deep-ITM put calendar converts a bullish view into low-margin, capped-risk exposure; roll-over cost (~₹3,500-4,000/month) is the real max risk.
Effective margin = gross margin minus next-day premium credit - check net, not gross, returns.

strategies.name: Deep-ITM put calendar (bullish, defined risk)
strategies.construction: Sell near-month 20,000PE (July), buy far-month 20,000PE (December), same strike
strategies.numbers: Entry 1 Jun: PoP ~70%; max profit ~₹23,000 (~55% of margin); roll cost ~₹3,500-4,000/month; gross margin ~₹43,000, net ~₹33,000; +₹6,000 (~20% RoC) after one month

strategies.adjustments: Roll monthly if strike not reached; each roll crystallizes ~₹3.5-4k cost
strategies.risks: Max loss ≈ cumulative roll costs (~₹20,000 over 5 months); loss if market collapses far below strike

quotes: I am neither a fundamental guy nor a technical guy - I am a techno-fundamental guy.
When you are inside the aeroplane you cannot see the aeroplane; step back to see the larger picture.

summary: Nifty +133; HDFC Bank +60 then -30 (DII profit-booking 340cr) while FII added 2,000cr; RIL and ITC took over support; 700 points in five sessions, ~2,000+ from 16,800; declares himself 'becoming a trend follower... LKG technical'; VIX spiked >10% on an up day (calls up, puts refused to fall) - called extraordinary; OI rotation out of 19,000/19,200 calls into 19,300/19,400; 19,300 PE heavy add; 20,000 by Deepavali possible.
lessons: VIX rising on an up day = nervous, hedged rally - option sellers beware even in uptrends
When VIX is low-to-rising and you're bullish, a put calendar beats a naked short put

summary: Sixth straight green for Bank Nifty but two-way violence: -97, +130, -50/60; consolidation with huge volatility as he predicted; Bajaj Finance monthly business update impressed; Hero MotoCorp back above 3,000 (2018 highs - Hero 3,500, Maruti 10,000 - still unrecovered); delivers the full margin math (75k span + 20k exposure; hedged span capped at max risk) explaining why far-hedge buying isn't margin-driven; far-put absurdity: 38,000 PE (7,000 OTM) at Rs 8-9; put calendar (his video idea) outperforming naked puts; VIX up again; FII 2,100cr, DII -800cr; warns 'vertical up moves reverse painfully'.
lessons: Margin arithmetic: hedged span is capped at max loss; beyond ~1,500 pts the hedge saves no margin - so far-OTM premiums are fear, not hedging
In rising-VIX regimes, calendars monetize theta-vol divergence that naked shorts cannot

summary: Rally against a global down day (Europe -2%); non-stop 16,800 to ~19,500 (~2,700 pts); July +500 in four sessions; FIIs: ~28,000cr in each of May and June (self-corrected figure), 8,000cr+ in early July; IT still 15-20% below highs - catch-up pending; caution triplet: VIX cooling after 2:30, futures premium compressed 90-100 → 35-40 pts, net institutional flow just 300cr (FII 2,600cr vs DII -2,350cr); put calendar (short Jul 20,000 PE, long Dec 20,000 PE) delivered; M&M + RIL = 65 of +100; auto index at ATH; OMC thesis (6 months of no price cuts + cheap Russian crude).
lessons: Exhaustion triplet: VIX cooling + futures-premium compression + slowing net flows = tighten risk even in uptrends
View can be right yet unprofitable - volatility structure (not direction) decides P&L; hence calendars

summary: The awaited correction: expected signs were PCR 1.45 and premium compression; morning Reliance-news spike took out yesterday's high (friends cut put calendars, benefited); 2:30-3:30pm swung +80 then -100; VIX notably did NOT spike - normal-correction pricing; strangle sellers profited; BSE Sensex option broker terminals failed three weeks running (a friend couldn't square up, heavy loss); IT sold; auto/PSU banks green; 'froth taken out'; FII +800cr vs DII -3,000cr; 19,000 = uptrend floor.
lessons: Markets react violently only to surprises; expected bad news (weak IT results) gets digested quietly
DII-heavy selling days gap less dangerously than FII-selling days - counterparty identity matters

summary: Nifty made fresh all-time high; expiry-day volatility punished intraday players; Bajaj Finance swung ~300 pts. Speaker recaps monthly consolidation ranges and notes Reliance ~40-50 pts from ATH, Infosys strong. FIIs +1,200 cr, DIIs -7 cr. Previews US/India inflation data and HCL Tech results. Suggests ITM put calendar as built-in stop-loss (max loss ~4,000-4,500/month) and ratio spreads.
lessons: In-the-money put calendar acts as a built-in stop-loss with capped monthly risk
Results-season last two weeks make markets choppy or trending - be careful

summary: Nasdaq 100 up ~50% in 9 months (10,500→15,500+); dollar index below 100 helping EMs. GIFT +50 after +80. Yesterday's Bank Nifty 500-pt fall unexplained against green global markets. Banking results next week (Bandhan today, HDFC Bank Monday, IndusInd Tuesday). lessons: Support and resistance matter mainly to options players, who build strategies around them
When a credit calendar turns debit, selling a strike at strong support restores the credit

summary: Expiry-day volatility; Dow's 13-session win streak; post-fall momentum thesis (Lehman/COVID +100% analogies; from 15,200 low only +30% so far, 20-30% more possible); trend past 17 weeks; 20-DMA held; box theory ladder to 20,000; deep-ITM put calendar strategy showcased (~50% return case); retail net-worth/ITR trading-bar rumor; 19,500-20,000 range.

Deep-ITM put calendars monetize a rising market with strictly limited downside

summary: Dow up 15 of 16 sessions; FIIs selling third day but dips bought. Framework: 3,000-pt rally came with only 250-300-pt dips - a 1,000-1,500-pt flush would be healthy. Deepavali target 20,000, December 21,000; recommends Aug-Dec 21,000 put calendar (max loss ~4,000). Titan tomorrow, SBI Friday.
lessons: Never buy all at once and never sell all at once - scale in and out so you keep riding an extended rally.
A five-week series with high OI at the box edges lets straddle sellers collect time value while the market chops inside its box.

summary: Designs long-dated (December) ratio structures for a slightly bearish view: buy 21,000PE, sell 3× 19,000PE, sell 2× 21,000CE (breakevens ~18,000/21,000, ~40% max profit, ~4%/month expected), plus the bullish mirror (1:4 call ratio with credit-fixing adjustments) and the combined non-directional version.
lessons: For a mildly directional multi-month view, deep-ITM long leg financed by ratio shorts beats naked option selling on margin and risk.
Equalize or over-cover naked legs with opposite-side shorts to shrink margin; add wings if unlimited risk is unacceptable.
Aim for ~4%/month on deployed capital - consistent with the ~30-40% p.a. realism ceiling.
Combine a call ratio and put ratio for a non-directional structure; book whichever leg is winning when the market stretches.

summary: Reviews five August 2023 paper trades: bearish Oct combo (+5% in 2 weeks), 2 Aug combo (+13-14% on Rs 1.27L margin), HNI-friend Bank Nifty book (+2% on ~Rs 60L), SBI results vol-crush strangle (+~10% on Rs 4.5L), and December long-term combos (+7% and +13% incl. a double-ratio). When the trend flips, close the old view - a bullish combo closed at +8% funded the bearish book.
Run double ratios (call ratio + put ratio) when direction is unknown; margin ~Rs 1.5L for ~13% in a month.
Review every posted trade publicly - wins and losses - to build trust.

summary: India VIX reads only ~1-month options, so June 2024's election-loaded IV was invisible in it: calls bid, puts sticky. His answer - a reversed deep-ITM put calendar (sell Feb 23,000PE, buy June 23,000PE for a net credit) that made ~25% on margin in ten sessions with defined risk.
lessons: India VIX is a one-month instrument - it cannot see IV built for events six months out; check the term structure yourself.
When far-month IV exceeds near-month IV, reverse the calendar: sell near, buy far.
Deep-ITM calendars behave like cheap hedges with tiny margin - ideal for event-loaded quarters.
Far-month event premium (June 2024 election) can make short-dated strangles bleed even as the market rises.

strategies.name: Reversed deep-ITM put calendar (bullish, event-premium harvest)

A repeated-tested resistance breaks hard once the trigger (results, flows) arrives; position before, not after.

Euphoric gaps are for selling hedges into, not for initiating longs

On binary days use system stop-losses with wide triggers; thin volume amplifies moves

summary: A quiet, classic expiry: after the gap-up was sold in 15 minutes, Nifty traded within ±20-25 points all day - ideal for option sellers. IT, FMCG, healthcare, consumer durables and pharma all hit ATHs - defensives lead while Bank Nifty sits ~5% under its high; that catch-up alone is ~1,000 Nifty points, making 26,000 a December possibility (euphoric stage). lessons: Quiet expiries are the straddle seller's harvest: low realised range plus fast theta.
Defensive-sector ATHs while the index heavyweight lags is the classic late-cycle rotation signature.
Index catch-up math: a lagging heavyweight's 5% gap equals ~1,000 points of stored index upside.

summary: Six major SEBI changes: contract size to minimum 15 lakhs, expiry rationalization, ELM on expiry day, upfront collection of premium, removal of calendar spread benefit on expiry

summary: US 6th straight up day; India tipped to be first US trade-deal signature; PM's defense meeting read as go-ahead for action; Bank Nifty beyond prior ATH zone; Reliance +8% (~20% off lows); weekly expiry opens violent for 30-45 min; exit put calendars before expiry day.
lessons: Weekly expiry opens violent for 30-45 minutes, then settles - but premiums are already gone; intraday expiry trading is structurally disadvantaged.
Exit put calendars a day before expiry: expiry-day margin spikes force unwinds.

summary: Teaches the call calendar: sell an ATM call in the near expiry, buy the same-strike call in a far expiry, after a very large market move (post ~1,000-point rally) when consolidation is likely. Demo: sold 24,900CE near-term at ~29, margin about 45-50K, capped loss near 10K; rolled weekly sales against one monthly long through June for about 11-12% on margin in three weeks.
lessons: After a very large single-direction move, markets statistically consolidate or drift slightly opposite - that is the calendar's home regime.
Call calendar = short near-dated call + long far-dated same-strike call: low margin (~50K vs ~1.7L for a naked straddle), limited but real loss if the trend extends.
Rolling the short leg weekly against a static monthly long harvests decay repeatedly; close only the short each week and re-sell.
Percentage returns look big on low-margin structures; judge risk by the capped loss, not the headline return.

strategies.name: Call calendar (with weekly rolling)
strategies.construction: Sell ATM call in nearest weekly expiry; buy same-strike call in far monthly expiry; on each weekly expiry, buy back the short and re-sell next week's ATM call
strategies.numbers: Example: sold 24,900CE ~Rs 29; monthly long same strike; margin ~Rs 45,000-50,000; modeled max loss ~Rs 10,000; June paper series: bought 25,000CE monthly, sold weekly 25,000CE (Jun 5, 12, 19) for ~Rs 5,800 total (~11-12% on margin in ~3 weeks)
strategies.best_regime: Immediately after a very large move (e.g., ~1,000 points in days) when consolidation with mild bias is expected
strategies.adjustments: If market trends strongly, the long leg cushions but does not eliminate loss; can widen strikes or roll the long leg; exit rather than average a losing calendar
strategies.risks: Loss if market trends strongly either way (limited on upside by the long call, but can exceed expectations intra-week); margin jumps if a strangle is added

quotes: Whenever the market makes a very big move, the probability of consolidation is very high
Margin 50,000 versus 1.7 lakh for a naked straddle - and the risk is limited

summary: Put-calendar variant: buy a put in the far monthly series, sell puts in near weekly expiries, rolling weekly; the net debit (July 25,000PE bought ~558 vs weekly sales ~319) was covered by selling an iron-strangle-style 24,000PE/26,000CE package (~350 collected). lessons: Put calendar mirrors the call calendar: long far-dated put, short weekly puts - harvest decay while keeping tail protection.
Calendars are net-debit structures; finance the debit by selling an adjacent strangle only if you also accept the larger margin that comes with it.
Rolling the short put weekly across a consolidating month compounds small wins: ~25% on margin in three weeks in the worked example.
Know your margin with and without the financing legs: 2 lakh with the strangle vs 70K without changes both risk sizing and return percentages.

strategies.adjustments: Close and re-sell the short put weekly; if range view fails, unwind the short strangle first to cut margin; roll the long put outward if the consolidation extends
strategies.risks: Sharp fall through the long strike late in the trade, or IV crush after event weeks; strangle legs add naked risk and margin

summary: Margin calculator walkthrough: futures margin (1.40 lakh) is not option margin (1.19 lakh for 10,000CE); span falls as strikes go further out while exposure stays constant; premium received is credited to ledger so effective margin is lower; hedged call+put together gets ~70,000 margin benefit.

Span margin shrinks as strikes go further out-of-the-money; exposure margin stays the same

quotes: If you put a stop loss, it is like slow poison. If you don't put a stop loss, it is like quick poison.

summary: Quantified case for taking long-term equity exposure via futures plus a debt collateral stack: ~Rs 7.5 lakh in Bharat Bond/FD earns ~Rs 50k interest while the long futures roll costs ~Rs 30k/year in premium - net ~Rs 10-20k saving vs cash buying; hedging via short call costs only incremental margin (~Rs 50k vs Rs 1.75 lakh); also covers lot-size, rollover and tax trade-offs.
lessons: For large capital, long futures funded by pledged debt instruments beats cash buying: interest income exceeds the cost-of-carry premium.
A short call against a long futures position needs only incremental margin - cash-market holders pay far more to run the same hedge.
Leverage is not inherently gambling: buying with Rs 100 while committing only Rs 20, keeping the rest safe, is capital efficiency.
Futures gains are business income (expenses deductible); cash equity gets 10% LTCG / 15% STCG - pick the instrument with the tax profile you prefer.

India options are European-style (exercise at expiry only); American-style allows any-time exercise.
quotes: Invest first, use it as collateral and do trading - the vice versa is not possible.

summary: P&L showcase: claims Rs 1.05 cr profit April-July 2020 on Rs 95 L capital (~110% in 4 months), Rs 66L April / Rs 10L May / -Rs 1.2L June / Rs 31L July; also claims Rs 47L profit during the March 2020 crash and Rs 1.55 cr over 10 months; closes with troll-defense and workshop-review promotion.
lessons: Option selling is a book of many trades: a few failures drown in the aggregate profit - the insurance-pool principle.
Adjustments and firefighting (not stop-losses) are how a losing view becomes a small profit or small loss.
Personal P&L screenshots are marketing, not evidence: audit capital trajectory and consistency, not single screenshots (inversion of the scam test).
quotes: I am not the god, I am just good.

summary: Q&A episode: expiry-day mechanics for hedged shorts (removing the long leg makes the short naked; index options cash-settle, stock options physically deliver if ITM - square off yourself); F&O ban-list illiquidity; advice to avoid stock F&O below ~1 crore capital and prefer indices; collateral eligibility (REC bonds, property, ELSS under 3 years ineligible); 50% cash margin component rule; Bharat Bond is cumulative, not annual-pay; option selling not advisable below ~10 lakh capital; no fixed timeline to become a successful trader.
lessons: Removing the protective long leg on expiry day converts your short into a naked position - margin and risk jump; close positions yourself rather than letting settlement decide.
Physical delivery applies only to stock F&O: short ITM call = give delivery, short ITM put = take delivery. Indices are cash-settled.
Collateral eligibility rule of thumb: anything not immediately liquidatable (property, REC/lock-in bonds, ELSS inside 3 years) cannot be pledged.
NSE margin rule: at least 50% of margin must be cash component - cash, FDs, liquid funds and Liquid BeES qualify; Bharat Bond counts as collateral, not cash.
quotes: Anything that cannot be liquidated immediately cannot be given as a collateral.

summary: Mechanics of the F&O ban (Market Wide Position Limit): MWPL = 20% of free-float market cap; a stock enters ban when combined open interest ends a day above 95% of MWPL; no fresh F&O positions next day (existing positions square-off only); ban lifts only when OI falls below 80%. Penalty for banned trading: 1% of contract value or 5,000 rupees, whichever is higher, capped at 1 lakh/day. Live examples: Vodafone Idea at 93.5% utilization, Canara Bank in ban at 88.5% (descending), Adani Enterprises at 88% not banned; nine stocks in ban for 12 August 2020.
lessons: MWPL math: 20% of free-float market cap caps total F&O open interest; speculative smallcaps hit it far sooner than large caps.
Ban asymmetry: entry at 95% utilization but exit only below 80% - ban lists persist for days and freeze hedgers mid-position.
During a ban you can only square off: no fresh futures or options positions, so adjustment trades become impossible exactly when risk peaks.
Trading a banned stock costs at least 5,000 rupees per lot (1% of contract value), capped at 1 lakh per day - plus unquantifiable exit-liquidity risk.
quotes: Usually the stocks that come under trading ban are the highly speculative stocks.

summary: Follow-up on the ITC call (bought ~198, now ~170, -15%): thesis unchanged - dividend yield above FD rates, effective cost cut below 170 by selling calls, patience and averaging down; high-dividend stocks are income plays, not momentum plays. New pick: BPCL - corrected from ~450-460 to ~350 on divestment delay; dividend yield ~4.65%; OMC earnings inversely track crude, and CME curves price crude flat (~$40-43) out to Dec 2022 and beyond. Entry paths: cash-secured puts (sold 350PE @14) or covered calls; full disclaimer.
lessons: Dividend-yield investing is a patience game: price declines raise the yield and attract institutions - the thesis strengthens as the price falls (if the dividend sustains).
Selling covered calls against a stock position lowers effective cost (bought ~198, effective <170) - income cushions drawdowns in non-momentum stocks.
Oil marketing companies profit inversely to crude: with CME curves flat near $40-43 out to 2022+, OMC earnings support is structural, not cyclical.
Event-delayed stocks (BPCL divestment) offer corrected entry points when the catalyst is deferred, not dead.

strategies.name: Cash-secured put entry on BPCL
strategies.construction: Sold BPCL 350PE at ~14 (August 2020 expiry), cash reserved for assignment
strategies.numbers: Collect 14/share/month; effective entry 336 if assigned
strategies.best_regime: Stock corrected on event delay; willing to own at strike
strategies.adjustments: Roll or take delivery and switch to covered calls
strategies.risks: Assignment in extended divestment delay / crude spike

strategies.name: Covered call on ITC
strategies.construction: Held ITC bought ~198; sold calls aggressively as price stalled
strategies.numbers: Effective cost below 170 after call income
strategies.best_regime: Range-bound high-dividend stock
strategies.adjustments: Continue rolling short calls; average down on dips
strategies.risks: Capped upside in a breakout; opportunity cost vs momentum stocks

quotes: The more the price goes down, the more the dividend yield - and more institutions will show interest.

summary: Introduces MCX BULLDEX bullion-index futures launched 24 Aug 2020: 70.52% gold / 29.48% silver weights, lot 50, monthly expiry, price ~16,000, contract ~8 lakh, margin ~6% (~48,000), tick 1. Frames gold as an inverse-correlation hedge and a pair-trading complement to equity positions.
lessons: Gold moves opposite equities over long cycles - 2008-2011 gold rose >400% post-Lehman while stocks crashed; 2020 COVID gold nearly doubled from the bottom.
A 10-20% bullion exposure lets equity shorts/longs be paired against gold positions as a cross-asset hedge.
New futures instruments can hedge equity portfolios at ~6% margin versus costly physical gold or gold ETFs.

strategies.name: Bullion index equity hedge
strategies.construction: Long/short equity portfolio paired with same-direction or inverse position in MCX BULLDEX futures (70.52% gold / 29.48% silver)
strategies.numbers: lot 50; ~16,000 index; ~8 lakh contract value; ~6% margin (~48,000); tick 1
strategies.best_regime: Portfolio-level diversification when equity-gold inverse correlation is intact
strategies.adjustments: Rebalance weights as gold/silver ratio drifts; roll monthly expiry
strategies.risks: Correlation breakdown; VaR-driven margin changes

quotes: When the markets are in bull mode, the gold will be in a bear mode. When the markets are in bear mode, the gold will be in a bull mode.

summary: Q&A episode: futures don't receive dividends but need lower margin for covered calls - buy cash only in dividend months; futures long + sold calls = covered-call income on dividend stocks. Trading-ban handling (reduce only, prefer large caps). Strike availability timeline (3 monthly + 10 weekly + long-dated). Portfolio-level stop loss (2% of capital) over per-trade stops. Deep/debt-fund-vs-FD and Japan's lost-decades questions.
lessons: Futures positions don't earn dividends but need only exposure margin for covered calls - hold futures normally, switch to cash in dividend-declaration months.
Set a portfolio-level stop (e.g. 2% of total capital across all positions) instead of mechanical per-trade stop losses.
Trade only Nifty/Bank Nifty or large caps - mid/small caps can hit F&O trading bans where you can only reduce positions.
No knowledge means risk in every market segment, not just options - bankruptcies happened in plain equities too.

strategies.name: Dividend-cycle futures + covered call
strategies.construction: Long futures on dividend-paying stock most of the year (cheap covered-call margin); switch to cash market only in dividend months
strategies.numbers: ITC cited with >5% dividend yield
strategies.best_regime: High-dividend-yield large caps with liquid options
strategies.adjustments: Time cash/futures switch to the dividend record period
strategies.risks: Futures basis/discount eats part of the dividend benefit

quotes: Small people look for opportunity. Big people create opportunity.
Stop loss is what you can afford to lose per trade - I keep a portfolio stop loss, not individual stop losses.

summary: Foundational lesson: derivatives defined via milk-to-butter and crude-to-petrol analogies; farmer price-realization origin story; >90% of Indian turnover is derivatives and Nifty is the world's most-traded contract; five derivative types; forward contracts taught through an exporter-student dollar exchange example.
lessons: A derivative's price is derived from an underlying - curd from milk, petrol from crude; keep the chain of derivation in mind
Derivatives began as farm price insurance (harvest-time glut) before entering financial markets after 1970
A forward fixes price today for a future exchange - each side eliminates the currency risk the other cannot bear
In India, derivatives turnover is 9x the cash market; Nifty is the world's most-traded derivative contract
quotes: Milk is the underlying, curd is the derivative; buttermilk is a derivative of curd

summary: Margin anatomy via a live Zerodha calculator: ACC long/short costs the same ~1.76 lakh (span 146,940 + exposure 29,000) against 8.5 lakh notional; stock-future margins vary with volatility (ACC ~21%, Adani Ent 47%, Ashok Leyland 35%); exposure margin fixed at 2% index / 3.5% stock; long/short terminology, MTM, squaring up, physical delivery.
lessons: Both long and short sides post margin to the exchange - it is a default fund, not a payment
SPAN (Standard Portfolio Analysis of Risk) scales with volatility; exposure margin is a fixed add-on (2% index, 3.5% stock futures)
Squaring up (counter-trade) before expiry removes any delivery obligation; most futures trades are speculative and never delivered
Volatile stocks demand much higher margins (47% vs 21%) - position size must respect the margin, not the notional
quotes: In futures you never buy or sell - you go long or short; both sides pay margin to the exchange

summary: RBI week ended with Nifty ~13,250-13,500; RBI's bar on HDFC Bank digital launches dented the heavyweight while PSU banks rallied on Ambani-insurance-sale hopes; cross-country check (Italy +26%, France +21%, Japan +15% in November) shows it was global liquidity, not MSCI; 12,800 = strong support; range 13,000-13,500.
lessons: When every country rallies together, attribute the move to the global tide (liquidity), not the local story.
VIX falling ahead of an event (premiums decaying into RBI) signals limited downside; fear priced out early is calm.

summary: Live firefighting case study: a short Bajaj Finance/Finserv future plus sold call went against the position as the stock jumped 5% (4,900 to 5,150). Rescue: laddered put sales (4,500/4,700/4,800/4,900/5,000/5,200 strikes), added long January future, sold 5,500 call; ~1 crore additional margin deployed; position closed +1.49 lakh. Plus market-order pattern and VIX-decay outlook.
lessons: Firefighting works only with reserve capital: this rescue needed roughly 1 crore against a 3.5-4 lakh drawdown.
Scale into rescue in ladders (multiple strikes/quantities), not one desperate ticket.
Converting a losing directional short into a hedged combo (long future + sold call + sold puts) can cap damage.
Intraday 100+ point falls that recover are put-selling windows; retail sells first, institutions stabilize.

strategies.name: Short-stock rescue ladder (firefighting)
strategies.construction: Short future + sold call went wrong; rescue = sold puts at 4,500/4,700/4,800/4,900/5,000/5,200 (4,500 qty total) + long Jan future + sold 5,500 call
strategies.numbers: Stock +250 (4,900->5,150); drawdown 3.5-4 lakh; ~1 crore extra margin; ~10 lakh margin per 1,000 qty; result +1.49 lakh
strategies.best_regime: When a short directional view is hit by a gap/momentum move you believe is temporary
strategies.adjustments: Ladder put sales into the spike, convert to hedged combo, keep averaging only with reserve capital
strategies.risks: Requires massive reserve margin; if the rally continues, losses compound - works only with deep pockets and fast execution

quotes: I am not a God - many times my view has gone terribly wrong; it is the money power and the adjustment plan that save the trade.

summary: Mission Options E07: explains put vs call etymology (put up for sale / call the price at auction), put option as car-insurance-like protection, breakeven = strike minus premium, and the probability-driven premium gradient across strikes using a cricket-betting analogy.
lessons: A put buyer gains the right to sell at the strike; breakeven is strike minus premium, mirroring the call's strike plus premium.
Premium falls as strikes move further out-of-the-money on both sides because the probability of reaching them falls.
Far OTM options are cheap lottery tickets - only justified when expecting an unusually large, fast move.
quotes: When the people buy, they call. When the people sell, they put.

summary: New-year P&L showcase across multiple family and company accounts summing ~7.52 crore for 2020, with posted 2020 targets (PMS/hedge-fund AUM 100 crore, training fee 1 crore, trading income 5 crore). Predominantly self-referential screen-share of broker back-offices; salvageable only for the corporate-vs-personal taxation point and self-competition message.
lessons: F&O profits above ~5 crore in a personal account can fall into the ~42% effective slab while a corporate structure is taxed at ~25% - entity choice materially changes post-tax returns.
Compete only with your own past self; benchmarking against rivals distracts from process.
quotes: There is only one person with whom I want to compete and his name is P R Sundar.

summary: Gold framework for India: local price = international dollar price x USD/INR + import duty. Duty went 1% (pre-2013) to 10% (2013) to 12.5% (2020), incentivizing smuggling. Since 1973 gold has spiked only three times - 1980 oil crisis, 2008-11 Lehman era to $1,910, 2020 COVID to $2,070 - and mean-reverts once each crisis resolves; calls $3,000 unlikely, advising against gold as an investment.
lessons: Indian gold price decomposes into international price x exchange rate plus import duty - all three must be judged before a view.
Gold spikes only around global crises (1980, 2008-11, 2020) and stalls for years once the crisis resolves - crisis premiums mean-revert.
Import duties high enough (12.5%) incentivize smuggling, which caps further hikes - a policy constraint for the duty trajectory.
A stable rupee removes gold's currency-hedge argument for Indian investors.
quotes: As and when there is a global crisis prices shoot up, as and when the global crisis is resolved... prices come down or stay flat.

summary: Q&A session: part-time-to-full-time trading transition, studies vs trading, when the 10% correction comes you won't dare to buy, hedge instead of exit, US markets and Bitcoin ('I do what I understand'), pledging stocks, option-selling margins under new rules, F&O income is business income.
lessons: People look for certainty in an uncertain market - that search itself is the mistake.
When the 10% correction finally comes, you will not dare to buy; investors need patience or hedges, not exits.
Trade only what you understand - the speaker avoids US markets and Bitcoin for this reason.
Option-selling profits are taxed as business income, not capital gains.
quotes: People are looking for certainty in an uncertain market. And that's a wrong thing.

summary: V-shape recovery day (~350 points) after Janet Yellen urged more COVID relief - bulls outnumbered bears and shorts ran. Demonstrated hedged call-selling: 14,700+ calls sold pre-rally lost little, 14,000-14,200 PEs sold on the flip profited. Bajaj Finance and Kotak short-covering ahead of results.
lessons: Short covering is mechanical: when news flips, the weak side runs and the crowd joins the beating.
Sell calls into falls and puts into rallies symmetrically - VIX declines cushion reversals.

summary: Both institutions sold together (two rowdies beating the common man): Bank Nifty fell ~1,800-1,900 points session-over-session; Nifty fell ferociously. Advised keeping a small short/hedge during extended rallies. Majority of the video: course/workshop announcements (₹5,000 iron-collar course; ₹24,999/₹49,999 workshops).
lessons: When both FII and DII sell together, retail has no institutional bid - respect the fall.
In extended bull runs, always carry a small short or hedge against coordinated profit-booking.

summary: GameStop/AMC short squeeze: retail Reddit crowd (WallStreetBets, ~4.5M members) forced hedge funds like Melvin Capital (reportedly -$5B) to cover; hedge funds sold other holdings to raise cash, creating a margin cascade that hit global markets; CBOE VIX jumped 63% in a day; Nifty -1,000 and Bank Nifty -3,000 in days; stay flat into the Feb 1 budget.
lessons: Short selling means selling shares you must borrow and return (SLB in India; borrowing in the US).
Hedge funds cover losses by selling other holdings - one squeeze can cascade into a whole-market margin call.
Low-float, heavily shorted names are ammunition for coordinated crowds; price can go 15x in two weeks.
When big institutions are endangered, exchanges and officials move to protect them - 'too big to fail' shapes crisis response.
quotes: Retail people came to know that these big funds have huge short positions... so we will buy these shares.

summary: Bank Nifty 'dream rally': +1,400 points vs Nifty +130-140; 30,000 (budget day) to 37,500 in ten sessions (+25%). Argues DIIs sell on mutual-fund redemption pressure from nervous retail; advises holding and hedging rather than exiting. Petrol-vs-Virat-Kohli-100 joke and 'PR Sundar indicator' joke (self-referential, drop).
lessons: Retail redemption pressure, not DII conviction, drives DII selling in melt-ups; exit via hedges, not selling long-term holdings.
Equity pays years of returns in a few weeks; missing those weeks is the real long-term risk.

summary: Consolidation (+20-25); Nifty held low, Bank Nifty broke it on Kotak -4%. Worry: Bitcoin -13.6% in two days (-20% swing) could force disorderly unwinding that bleeds into equities (GameStop hedge-fund spillover parallel). Reliance O2C demerger supported Nifty; yesterday's stock picks (BPCL, IOC, ITC) rose. FII -1569, DII +216 (first DII buying in a long time).
lessons: A disorderly unwind in any asset class hits equities first - watch correlated leverage, not just one market.
Average-in via put sales at value zones; Buffett's greedy-when-fearful frame operationalized.

summary: Vindication of an Aug-2020 'gold peaked' call: gold below $1,700 vs Bank of America's $3,000/18-month forecast. Gold's Indian price = international price × USDINR × import duty. 2013-21 jewellery gold (~₹3,000 to ~₹4,500/g) underperformed bank FDs; duty cut 12.5% to 10% in Budget 2021.
lessons: Indian gold price decomposes into international price × USDINR × import duty - all three must align to rally.
From 2013 to 2021 jewellery gold returned ~50%, less than a bank FD - hedge, not compounding asset.
Gold hedges inflation and currency risk; with a stable rupee and rising rates expected, the hedge was cheap to skip.
Higher duty widens the smuggling arbitrage; the 2021 cut to 10% narrowed it.
quotes: Gold is for the beauty you enjoy, not the returns you expect.

summary: Q&A batch: no-goals/process philosophy; cyclical-defensive and growth-value bull-bear mapping; cross-hedging equities with gold; implied volatility (individual) vs VIX (collective); ITC as dividend-plus-covered-call income (12-13% p.a.); valuation beats sector prediction; embracing uncertainty.
lessons: Process is more important than the product - outcomes are noise, method is signal.
Bull markets favour growth and cyclicals; bears favour defensives - but exceptions (2008-14 pharma) are common.
Implied volatility is per-stock or per-contract; VIX is the index-level aggregate of expectations.
Dividend yield plus covered-call writing can stack to low-double-digit returns on sleepy large caps.
