quotes: People expect certainty in an uncertain market - the one thing it will never give.

summary: Fed held rates near zero through 2023; speaker rebuts taper-tantrum-2021 fears with a 2013-vs-2021 audit: 2013 saw rupee 53→69 (~40% depreciation in months), Chidambaram's gold import tax 1%→10%, Nifty -20%, LIC buying at 5,150; 2021 shows no FII selling (net positive despite ~900-pt fall), strong rupee (69→72.5 over 8 years), record ~$550B FX reserves. Verdict: bull-market correction, near bottom; Nasdaq the global weak link; Reliance 2,200→2,000; ITC +7-8% on demerger; BoB 100→70.
lessons: Auditing the prior crisis against today's plumbing (reserves, flows, currency) is how you size - or dismiss - the repeat risk.
Corrections: buy stocks at 10-15% off, indexes at 8-10%, hedge with options, average down one tranche later.

summary: The canonical failure arc: buy stagnant stocks, jump to leveraged futures, blow up on an un-hedgeable news gap, chase guru software and 'position sizing' gyan, end up paying trainers from the last 10% of capital. Stocks move 90% in 10% of the time.
lessons: A stock makes 90% of its move in 10% of the time - boredom is the price of holding (Reliance flat 2008-2017, then +400% in 3 years; a power stock flat a decade, then 3x in 3 months).
10x leverage cuts both ways: +1% becomes +10%, but a 5% news gap on 9 lots erases half the capital overnight.
The last-10%-capital recovery mindset is fatal: gamblers who try to win back the final 10% lose that too.
Trainers monetize the desperate: overpriced software (Rs60,000/yr, Rs30,000 commission) and fictitious model portfolios (Rs3L to Rs40L, '2000%') target people who just lost 90%.
quotes: If you want to become a doctor you study five years, an engineer four - how do you come to the stock market without studying?
You should have thought about recovery before losing the 90%, not after.

summary: Maharashtra COVID restrictions triggered knee-jerk Monday selloff: Nifty -400, Bank Nifty -1,500 intraday, India VIX +15% at worst; markets recovered 200+ points intraday. Speaker called it an overreaction given vaccine availability and strong US jobs (+916k).
lessons: Markets move violently only on surprise news; the same shock repeated gets a muted reaction.
In hedged positions, square off the sold leg's offset first - unwinding in the wrong order makes the short naked and margin explodes.

summary: Continues the leveraged-trader parable: cutting to 2 lots makes a 10% win worth only 2% of capital - so sizing alone solves nothing. The real answer is diversification across strategies, strikes and timeframes, like splitting money across business, FD, equity, gold and property.
lessons: There is no universal 'right' position size: 9 lots risks ruin, 2 lots makes wins trivial - sizing rules alone do not create returns.
Diversify across strategies, strike prices and timeframes; that is how 80-90% of capital stays deployed without concentrated blow-up risk.
Run capital like a business portfolio: business, FD, equity, gold, property - each leg rescues or funds the others in trouble.
A contrarian in a room of nineteen is either too stupid or too intelligent; only results distinguish them (Thyrocare founder's verdict, 2018).
quotes: Everyone wants to be different from others, but nobody wants to think different from others.
Whatever people do in the stock market, everything is wrong.

summary: India's managed-money menu: MFs (any amount, cash-only, 1:1 hedging, now covered calls on Nifty-50 stocks), PMS (Rs50L min, 2%+20%, micro-caps), AIF Cat-III (Rs1Cr min, F&O allowed, rare). Hedge defined honestly: a compound wall, not a bunker - and insurance you buy at entry, not after a 50% fall.
lessons: A hedge is a compound wall, not a bunker: it converts unlimited loss into limited loss; 100% hedging produces 0% return.
Buy insurance when you buy the car: hedge at position open, never after the share has already fallen 50%.
Vehicle fees shape risk-taking: MFs (1-1.5%) stay plain; PMS (2% + 20%) chase micro-caps; only AIF Cat-III may use F&O - and few exist.
Mutual funds may hedge 1:1 (short futures equal to holdings) and recently sell covered calls on Nifty-50 stocks only.

strategies.name: Protective put (vehicle-insurance hedge)
strategies.construction: Long shares (e.g. Reliance at 2,000) + buy 1,900 put
strategies.numbers: Max loss ~Rs100/share plus premium instead of Rs1,000 in a black-swan fall to 1,000
strategies.best_regime: Any long equity position opened with event/earnings risk ahead
strategies.adjustments: Roll the put on rallies; ladder strikes for cheaper protection
strategies.risks: Premium drag; protection only while held

quotes: Hedging does not mean there will be no loss - it means the loss is limited.
100% hedging will give you only 0% return.

summary: 'Perfect storm' Monday: headline-driven selloff (record 2.75 lakh daily cases, remdesivir black market, HDFC Bank miss, bitcoin crash). Nifty low 14,213 (his 14,200 support held), then +160 recovery; Bank Nifty -1,500 intraday, +900 recovery. OI analysis failed - put writers squared up to hedge, cascading the fall. FII -1,633 cr, DII +2,355 cr.
lessons: In panic-hedging regimes, open-interest analysis breaks down - crowd positioning stops predicting.
When headlines drive the market, ignore global cues for a few days and trade the news cycle.

summary: Explains why Indian hedge funds (AIF Category III) barely exist: 2x leverage cap computed on contract value, not margin, makes option-selling strategies uneconomic; plus tax asymmetry - F&O profits taxed yearly while cash-market losses only offset cash gains, so tax can exceed net profit.
lessons: Regulating leverage on contract value rather than margin makes premium-selling strategies economically unviable inside funds.
India taxes F&O profits in the year earned but cash-equity losses only offset cash gains for 8 years - hedged portfolios can owe tax exceeding net profit.
The managed-account grey area exists because licensed vehicles are unviable; giving someone trading password is at your own risk.

summary: Error-trade post-mortem: two mis-keyed legs (meant 33,200/33,700 puts, sold calls) left ~6,000 short calls into a 1,000-point Bank Nifty rally; panicked firefighting (10k-12.5k lots) using SEBI's one-time extra intraday margin; 26-lakh MTM loss rescued to +45,000 by close. Argues one-time intraday leverage should stay; peak-margin rules enable broker abuse. Announces pre-market report launch + sponsor teaser.
lessons: Fat-finger errors happen to professionals: pre-planned repair (hedge with puts, use emergency margin) beats panic booking.
Peak-margin rules create arbitrage for dishonest brokers - reconcile ledgers and escalate to SEBI with proof.

summary: ~300-point high-to-low fall on US CPI fear; US April CPI printed 4.2%, highest in ~13 years. He closed all positions into the Friday holiday. India data was strong: CPI 4.29%, IIP +22.4%, GST 1.4 lakh crore - regime flipped to good local cues, bad global cues. Three-month range 14,200-15,400.
lessons: Go flat into a binary macro event when the tail risk is a 10%-type session - losing 5-10 points of edge is cheap insurance.
Rangebound markets reward monthly short straddles; trend traders starve, sellers eat.

summary: Sponsored explainer of theme-based basket investing: curated stock baskets by theme (rural demand, dividend yield, all-weather), one-click execution, periodic rebalancing, SIP support, and costs vs mutual funds and DIY buying.
lessons: Theme baskets let you express a macro view (good monsoon -> rural demand -> FMCG and two-wheelers) more precisely than a mutual fund.
All-weather allocation pairs equity with debt (stability) and gold (inverse correlation) as a built-in hedge.
Rebalancing keeps a basket true to its thesis - weight shifts or constituent swaps are decided by rule, not emotion.
Direct stock-picking for novices is the ladies-finger problem: self-selection picks the worst ones; curated baskets or funds reduce it.
quotes: Trading is for making money. Investment is for creating wealth.
Gold is usually inversely correlated with equity market. So it is a hedge to each other.

summary: Curriculum episode on exercise and assignment: CE/PE naming reflects European style, exercise pays only intrinsic value, assignment is random among sellers, and European-style cash-settled index options exist to keep hedging stable.
lessons: Exercise pays only intrinsic value - selling the option in the market usually fetches more, so exercise only when liquidity dies.
Indian options are European style (hence CE/PE); American-style exercise existed decades ago (PA/CA era).
Only in-the-money options can meaningfully be exercised; out-of-the-money exercise pays zero.
Under American style, random assignment can strip a covered call's hedge mid-cycle - the structural flaw European style fixes.
quotes: Exercise, assignment will happen only at the intrinsic value.
American options can be exercised at any point of time even before expiring, whereas European option can be exercised only at the end of expiry.

summary: Day of surprises: gap-up sustained to close 15,690; VIX -8.5% near 15; mystery 15,700PE (bought ~350) expired at ₹10 — 'boys vs men' conviction lesson; first expiry under new margin regime (0.33x broker extra-margin); IndusInd -7% on one-year-old Hinduja Cayman news, recovered above 1,000.
lessons: At all-time highs, stale rumors trigger violent sell-offs — keep hedges in place. Conviction means positioning on your view, not just predicting.

summary: RBI policy day (expected non-event, comments watched); tech→non-tech global rotation; Bank Nifty still ~2,000 points below Feb high while Nifty above it — PSU catch-up could drive 16k; FII long >85% five straight sessions; 16,000 highest call OI; US jobs data tonight.
lessons: Every dip is a buy while put-writing conviction holds — but always hedge positions at all-time highs. Highest-OI reads are muddied by margin-motivated combos.

summary: Rupee hit 74.25 triggering FII-repatriation panic; Nifty -300 from high breaking 15,500, Bank Nifty -900 intraday, then +250 recovery; end-day FII bought 2,680cr (3x the prior day's sell); Kotak call ladder and LIC put-loss-offsetting shown live.
lessons: Rupee slides when FIIs repatriate - a falling rupee in a falling market signals exit, not rotation, and self-fulfills more selling.
Offset feared delivery: a losing put can be neutralized by selling calls higher up (his LIC hedge ladder).
The Einstein-driver joke: when risk hits your face, you must know your escape - plan exits before entry.

summary: Argues options trading is ethical: derivatives exist to transfer risk (insurance analogy), the product itself isn't gambling though people gamble with it; ~7,000 listed stocks but only 200–250 in F&O, so non-F&O holders hedge via Nifty/Bank Nifty.
lessons: Option selling is the insurance business: risk is transferred from hedger to risk-taker for a premium.
Nothing is inherently gambling; purpose (hedging) vs misuse (speculation) are different users of the same tool.
Only 200–250 of ~7,000 listed stocks have F&O; other portfolios hedge through index options.
Gamblers exit broke, but new gamblers keep arriving — that cycle, not the instrument, is the harm.
quotes: Sellers take your risk the way an insurer takes your family's risk — for a premium.
A matchstick can light a candle or burn a house; the fault is in the hand, not the stick.

summary: Fed dot plot signalled two 2022 hikes; Nifty fell ~300 intraday Friday then recovered ~250 on puzzling FII data; ~₹5,000 cr SBI block deal (TA Associates seller, Morgan Stanley Asia Singapore buyer); Dow -500 on quadruple witching; range 15,500-16,000.
lessons: Professional option sellers avoid holding into expiry week — gamma makes hedges and stops unreliable.
At all-time highs 5-10% corrections are routine; bull-market corrections are fast and furious.

summary: Rally despite flat open; double-top reframed: repeated 15,900 visits weaken it - a break implies 400-500 pt rally; FII data delayed; 15,800PE / 16,000CE max OI; cabinet-reshuffle scare - he hedged overnight, recalling May-2019 Bank Nifty -1,000 pts in seconds on Sitharaman FM appointment; reshuffle proved minor/non-event; metals up, autos down.
lessons: Political appointment of the finance minister is a high-impact, fast-reversal market event.
Repeated tests of a level weaken it; breakouts arrive when crowded positioning is wrong.

summary: Tokyo COVID emergency before Olympics + China tech crackdown hit Asia; consolidation math: 11 Jun 15,800 = 8 Jul 15,800 (20 sessions flat); TCS results today - plans 3,250 straddle and 3,100PE/3,400CE strangle unhedged (IV crush play); FII bought 533cr Wednesday; 7 heavyweight stocks ~50% of Nifty weight - sell their calls when bearish; Reliance stuck ~2,100.
lessons: A month-long consolidation resolves violently - prepare for both directions.
Selling options on index heavyweights beats index options when direction conviction is high (richer premiums).

summary: How Indians can access US equities: LRS forbids offshore derivatives, cash equity allowed but shares are expensive; proposes an ETF-based global allocation (half India, half NASDAQ) that doubles as a rupee-depreciation hedge.
lessons: Indian tax residents cannot trade derivatives in any foreign market under LRS - cash equity is the legal route.
US mega-cap share prices (lakhs per share) lock out small investors; index ETFs solve ticket-size and selection risk.
A US allocation is a natural hedge: if the rupee depreciates, dollar assets gain even when the share price is flat.
Splitting equity 50% India / 50% NASDAQ 100, with the India half split across large- and next-50 index ETFs, balances beta.

strategies.name: Global 50/50 ETF allocation (as promoted via smallcase)
strategies.construction: 50% Indian equity ETFs (25% Nifty 50 ETF + 25% Nifty Next 50 ETF) + 50% NASDAQ 100 ETF; SIP-able; quarterly rebalance
strategies.numbers: minimum ticket ~1,509 rupees; claimed 8.5% in first 5 months
strategies.best_regime: long-term wealth building with currency-hedge overlay
strategies.adjustments: periodic rebalancing restores target weights automatically
strategies.risks: US drawdowns, no derivatives hedging allowed offshore

quotes: The power of the crocodile is only inside the water - we understand our companies better than any foreigner does.

summary: Markets closed at swing low after Nifty -270 and Bank Nifty -660 for the week; ICICI results reaction, OI map (put 10,000/call 11,000) and Nov range 9,500-10,500 proposed; 9,951 (March low) named as the line in the sand.
lessons: Rallies on heavyweights: ADR read-through (ICICI +4.8% in US) signals ~200 pts Bank Nifty contribution next day.
Have a hard invalidation level (previous correction low) and exit all bullish bets below it.

summary: FII selling of 1,500cr+ broke Bank Nifty below 26,000; Nifty -300 in three days despite good rupee (<71) and benign crude. 'Two rowdies' analogy: retail aligned with FIIs against DIIs. Cash-market FII buying returned late. Pre-holiday long weekend (US closed for Thanksgiving, local holiday) pushed traders to square off.
lessons: Ahead of long weekends traders refuse to carry positions - square-off flows amplify moves.

summary: Against unanimous retail bearishness in COVID: lead-vs-lag indicators, the good/very-good/bad/very-bad news quadrant, consensus danger, efficient markets ('you are last to know'), and why heavy put buying at high premium is a losing game.
lessons: Markets price the lead indicator (next few months) - current bad news is already in the price (efficient market: you are last to know).
Very good news invites profit booking; very bad news invites policy rescue - so both can be sell/buy signals respectively.
Consensus is dangerous: when every retail message is bearish, the short trade is already crowded.
Defensive sectors (FMCG/IT/pharma) can rally through market-worst periods - index-level gloom hides stock-level bull markets.
quotes: Good news is a good news; very good news is a bad news. Bad news is a bad news; very bad news is a good news.
You are the last one to know the fact - whatever is in the public domain is already factored into the market.

summary: Explains the historic negative WTI print: contracts marked for physical delivery with storage full forced holders to pay to exit, driving May-2020 futures to -$37 while June contracts stayed normal. Analogy-driven, with explicit disclaimers.
lessons: Contracts expiring into physical delivery can print absurd prices when storage is exhausted - know delivery mechanics before holding.
Negative prices were contract-specific: the next-month contract kept trading at normal positive levels.
quotes: Storage facilities are completely full, no more storage is possible, and that created a huge panic among the buyers.

summary: IndusInd Bank profit fell 77% but stock closed ~15-17% higher because market expected 95% fall - expectation vs absolute drives expiry-day moves. Precedent: Bank of Baroda +25% after worst-ever loss. Teaches adjustment philosophy and the bus/pothole analogy.
lessons: Prices move on results versus expectations, not on absolute results - better-than-feared can rally
On expiry day, stocks can move opposite to results as shorts cover
Never copy someone's strategy blindly unless you have their capital and skills (bus-pothole analogy)
Without extra capital and adjustment skills, your only tool is a stop-loss in your mind

strategies.name: IndusInd earnings-day iron-fly style combo
strategies.construction: Sell 400CE + sell 400PE, buy 500CE + buy 300PE (current month)
strategies.numbers: profit down 77% vs expected 95% fall; stock closed ~15-17% higher
strategies.best_regime: earnings day when heavy short positioning built up
strategies.adjustments: speaker's own adjustments not disclosed; states adjustments depend on additional capital
strategies.risks: big gap moves on expiry; adjustments need reserve capital

quotes: It is not the 50,000 or the 500 - it is what you get versus your expectation.
You cannot just follow somebody blindly unless you have the same capability of the person you are following.

summary: Argues index options beat stock options: indices cannot crash 50-60% in a day (DHFL -65%, Infibeam -70% did), index margins are half of stock margins for similar contract size, far-strike liquidity is deep, no physical delivery, panic exits always available.
lessons: Return on margin matters, not how much the underlying moves - index gives 6-7% on margin vs 4% for a stock moving twice as much
Stocks can gap 50-70% overnight; indices are circuit-protected
Index options keep liquidity in far strikes and later months; stock options do not
No physical delivery headache in index options
quotes: At the end of the day, what matters is the return on our investment. It is not how many percent the underlying moves.

summary: Explains the 8,950PE flash spike (0.50 to ~20 in minutes) as a probable fat-finger market buy, citing the earlier NSE episode where a broker's basket-order error crashed Nifty ~15% before reversal; notes May's three weekly expiries all closed within 9,100-9,200 despite violent daily swings; then unpacks why Reliance's rights entitlement traded 30-40 above intrinsic (staggered 25/25/50 payment schedule).
lessons: Resting limit orders far from spot can get filled by flash spikes; square off immediately - such dislocations vanish in seconds and cannot be systematically captured.
A month can be violently volatile intraday yet flat close-to-close: distance-based option selling harvests the chaos.
Staggered-payment instruments (rights entitlements) can rationally trade above intrinsic because of embedded financing value.
quotes: Sometimes the market is like a beach horse: it runs around, but always returns to the same spot.

summary: Bullish call vindicated: Nifty 9,000->10,200 in ~7 sessions as FIIs turned daily buyers; US May payrolls +2.5M vs -8M expected sent Nasdaq to ATH; recounts Nov-2018 elections->Balakot FII cycle; NSE option-price glitch Thursday hurt traders.
lessons: Don't be a bull or a bear - be a chameleon; markets change trend when everyone leans one way.
Always trade with the trend; fighting it with leverage (F&O) makes losses heavy.

summary: Teaches synthetic futures: long = buy ATM call + sell ATM put; short reversed. Demonstrates on June futures that synthetic replicates futures payoff (-219 vs -222) while letting MTM losses sit against collateral, cutting STT/stamp-duty base ~25x, and reaching Dec-expiry exposure without rollovers.
lessons: Synthetic long = buy ATM call + sell ATM put; replicates the futures payoff almost exactly.
Futures MTM losses must be paid in cash; synthetic-option MTM can rest against collateral until booked.
Charges apply on premium (about 30,000) instead of contract value (about 7.5 lakh) - roughly 25x lower cost base.
Synthetics reach 6-8 month expiries without the three-month futures rollover treadmill.

strategies.name: Synthetic futures (long/short)
strategies.construction: Long: buy ATM call + sell ATM put (same expiry). Short: reverse legs
strategies.numbers: Demo: June futures -222 vs synthetic -219 on a 222-point fall; cost base 7.5 lakh (futures) vs ~30,000 (synthetic) per lot at Nifty 10,000, lot 75
strategies.best_regime: Any directional view where collateral efficiency matters; far-month exposure
strategies.adjustments: Exit both legs together; unbalanced exit leaves a naked leg with higher margin
strategies.risks: Stock synthetics fail on deep-ITM liquidity; index only

quotes: Buy at the money call option and sell at the money put option - the effect is exactly the same as long in futures.

summary: India-China border clash hits mid-session: Bank Nifty gap-up 700 then -1200 then +600 whipsaw; Nifty -150 from highs. Speaker argues knee-jerk not war: no firing, stone-pelting clash; option premiums stayed calm - the market's own verdict; Reliance hit all-time high; buy-the-dip framing.
lessons: If option premiums do not rise on bad news, the market is pricing a knee-jerk, not a trend change.
A country already fighting a pandemic will not open a second front; separate sentiment shock from fundamental risk.
Geopolitical gap-downs in stocks on your radar are entries, not exits, when premiums stay calm.
quotes: Smart people will not have more than one enemy at a time.

summary: Post-rally consolidation view: support 9,900, resistance 10,700; Fed restricted bank buybacks (Dow -700 Friday); ITC results in line; data week ahead (auto sales, China/India PMI, US payrolls Thursday).
lessons: After a 1,000-point monthly rally, expect 1-2 weeks of range consolidation, not continuation.
Central-bank restrictions on one sector (bank buybacks) can drag the whole US tape overnight.

summary: Counters technical analysts calling for a 7500 retest: after the October 2008 Lehman low (2252), Nifty doubled within a year and the low was never retested; the COVID candle's high was 11400 - once crossed, it may never be retested. COVID fell less than 50% (vs 2008's >50%), so recovery may be slower, but 15000 arrives before 7500. Investment timing: invest when you have surplus cash; exit when you need the money.
lessons: Post-crash lows of true panic candles (2008, 2020) are historically not retested once the recovery candle's high is crossed - drawdown bottoming behaves asymmetrically.
The depth of the crash sets the pace of recovery: 2008's >50% fall doubled in a year; 2020's shallower fall implies a slower but persistent recovery.
The right time to invest is when you have surplus cash; the right time to exit is when you need the money - waiting for the 'right opportunity' is itself a losing strategy.
quotes: the right time to invest is when you have surplus cash. The right time to exit is when you need the money

summary: Counters the 'invest for long term' reflex: Nifty top-50 averaged ~11x over 1994-2020 (doubling slower than 6 years) while risk-free debt doubled in ~6; only stock-pickers or entry-exit timers should invest; Anil Ambani group stocks lost 95-99%.
lessons: Nifty top-50 average return 1994-2020 did not double in 6 years, underperforming risk-free debt instruments doubling in ~6.
Index survivorship inflates returns: failing companies are ejected, so you average only the winning horses.
Stock market suits only stock-pickers or those who time entries and exits; passive buy-and-hold is sold as a myth.
quotes: Stock market is only for two people: those who can pick the stock that performs, or those who know when to get in and out.

summary: Explains SEBI's cash-market margin changes effective 1 August 2020: upfront margin now required even to sell shares already held, because the exchange cannot distinguish intraday sells from delivery sells. Walks through VaR+ELM+additional margin arithmetic (Reliance ~22%, SBI ~35%, Idea ~77.5%), T+2 settlement, early pay-in, and the auction market for short deliveries; predicts movement toward T+1.
lessons: Intraday margin scales with stock volatility: roughly 4.5x leverage on Reliance (~22%) but barely 1.3x on Idea (~77.5%) at the time.
From August 2020, selling shares you already hold also requires margin in the account - the exchange cannot tell an intraday sell from a delivery sell.
Settlement mechanics: T-day trade, T+1 funds/shares to broker/exchange, T+2 demat/money transfer; early pay-in avoids the shortfall but forfeits the auction-market rescue for short deliveries.
A broker without early pay-in can cover a client's accidental short delivery via the auction market - the auction price risk falls on the client.
quotes: Anything that cannot be liquidated immediately cannot be given as a collateral.

summary: After Nifty corrected 11,800 to ~11,200 and Bank Nifty 3,000+, asks crash vs correction: March 2020 crashed with VIX spiking 15 to 85; this fall came without a VIX spike or negative news - US tech profit-booking (Tesla -21%, Apple -6%, Dow -650, Nasdaq into correction). Newton's first law framing: falls continue till an external force (big buyer) intervenes; bought ITC averaging down at 183.
lessons: Crash requires a VIX spike tied to negative news; a fall without VIX expansion is profit booking and tends to stabilize.
Newton's first law for markets: trends persist until an external force - watch for the big buy order that arrests a fall.
Once a 15-30% correction makes prices attractive, new buyers arrive and markets stabilize - sell-offs without news are opportunities, not exits.
quotes: If the bigger crash has to come, the volatility index has to shoot up. Right now it is not shooting up as much as people are expecting.

summary: Carry trade taught through a 1990s anecdote: borrow at 3% abroad, deposit at ~19.5% NRI rates in India - ₹10L became ₹25L in six years, netting ~₹13.75L. Risks: access and currency (1991's ~20% two-day devaluation). Foreigner's-eye math: Nifty 6,000→12,000 (2008-20) is 100% in rupees but ~10% in dollars at ₹40→₹75. Weak DXY = foreign tailwind.
lessons: FII returns are rupee returns discounted by currency: a 100% index gain can be ~10% in dollars if the rupee slides 40→75.
Carry profits die by devaluation, not by rates - always price the currency leg before the yield leg.
Weak dollar index = double benefit for foreign money (market return + currency); strong dollar = double whammy exit.
quotes: For you the return is 100 percent; for the foreigner it is hardly 10 percent - that is the currency effect.

summary: The Robinhood phenomenon mapped to India: 300% jump in Zerodha's new demat accounts, 2.6M CDSL accounts since March (record 8,30,405 in June vs ~3L/month in FY20), retail at 68% of cash volumes - a decade high. Cautionary anchor: Nikkei 40,000 (1989) still ~half after 30 years; Shanghai never reclaimed its pre-Lehman 6,000 in 12 years; skills before size.
lessons: Record account openings mark euphoria tops more than opportunities - the wave that lifts markets also supplies its exits.
A market can stay below its high for decades (Nikkei 1989, Shanghai 2007) - 'it always comes back' is survivorship folklore.
Acquire skill before size: the lockdown cohort learned trading from YouTube tutorials with pandemic savings.
quotes: The market can stay below its peak for thirty years - make sure you acquire skills before you commit money.

summary: Post-market analysis of a 300-point Nifty fall: Supreme Court loan-moratorium interest-on-interest uncertainty hit Bank Nifty (-1,150 from high), US stimulus stalemate, France/UK COVID restrictions; uses Sep-24 expiry analog to frame next-day scenarios and S&P 500 VIX ~29-30 as exit trigger.
lessons: Policy uncertainty without a verdict is what markets fear; the RBI/Supreme Court moratorium case kept banks under pressure
HDFC Bank's index weightage is so large that a 10-rupee move shifts Bank Nifty ~200 points
Compare the current session to a recent structurally similar session (Sep-24 expiry) to script next-day scenarios
When S&P 500 VIX crosses ~30, it is time to close positions
quotes: If S&P 500 VIX is crossing 30, then it is time to close the positions

summary: IPO vs OFS explainer: IPO money goes to the company; OFS is an existing shareholder (Government) selling. Walks through applying via a broker's online console (corporate actions > OFS > cutoff price for retail <2 lakh). IRCTC context: 2019 IPO at 320, rallied ~600% to ~2,000, OFS floor 1,367.
lessons: In an OFS the company gets nothing - an existing shareholder is exiting, so the process and risks differ from an IPO.
Retail applicants (<2 lakh) should bid at cutoff price to avoid being priced out.
A hot prior IPO listing does not guarantee OFS profits - IRCTC had corrected ~15% into the OFS.
quotes: An OFS is one shareholder offering his shares for sale - the company does not receive the money.

summary: Bank Nifty ~31,000 carried by HDFC Bank and Kotak alone; HDFC, Bajaj Finance, Divi's Labs at fresh highs. 'Never short a stock crossing its ATH in a bull market.' Tata Power parable: 10 years zero return, then +300% in three months - foreshadows his 'Nifty to 25,000' thesis (2003 analogy). Bajaj Finance short rescued via quick reaction (+5.28L total, >5% gain on a wrong view). US stimulus and Georgia Senate race (5 Jan) flagged as next triggers.
lessons: React fast when a trade goes wrong - flexibility beats being branded a permanent bull or bear.

summary: V-recovery: Nifty 13,200→13,620 and Bank Nifty 29,000→30,000 in one session as Brexit deal and France-UK port news lifted Europe. Sold 13,000 PEs with conviction through the fall. IT stocks at ATHs on Accenture read-through; Reliance alone could add ~500 Nifty points reclaiming 2,400.
lessons: Conviction, not just knowledge or technicals, is what makes money through drawdowns.
Bull-market profit-booking is frequent because so many ride profits - corrections are structural.

summary: COVID-strain Monday: Nifty >500 intraday fall, Bank Nifty −1,500, then three-day rebound; week closed near prior close. Year-end: FII volumes −30–40%, holiday lull. OI: 13,500 PE / 14,000 CE max. Brexit deal done. Range call 13,500–14,000; sold calls >14,000, puts <13,500.
lessons: Bull-market corrections are fast and furious — and can recover with the same speed.
Holiday-week volume is insignificant, so price action in it should also be treated as insignificant.

summary: All-time-high day (~13,900 future) after Brexit deal signed, Trump signed stimulus, vaccine-efficiency news. Delivered the 'everything people do in the market is wrong' monologue: no training culture, 'which share will go up?', 95% failure ignored, business has no predetermined stop-loss.
lessons: Nobody starts a restaurant with a predetermined stop-loss - diagnose, adjust, and only quit when it is genuinely not your cup of tea.
95% of investors and 99% of traders lose, yet everyone wants to trade - question the base rate before entering.

summary: Defines the three market cycles - bull, bear and sideways ('bunny') - and price correction vs time correction; shows Nifty 2003-07 4-6x bull, then 2008-2020 as India's longest consolidation where even 13 years of index gains lost to bank FDs; Chennai builder parable about exploiting cycle ignorance.
lessons: Sideways markets are a 'time correction' - with opportunity cost included, flat index years can underperform bank FDs.
2003-2007 delivered a 4-7x bull; 2008-2020 was the longest consolidation in Indian market history - cycles, not linearity, are the norm.
Only experts capture cycle turning points (builder parable): amateurs hold through stagnation; insiders engineer exits at the top.
quotes: In any field only the smart people can make fantastic money.

summary: Bond pricing via a non-callable FD analogy: accreted interest raises fair value over time; when market rates rise, existing bonds trade cheaper (yield up); when rates fall, they trade at premium (yield down). Live examples: Bharat Bond 2030 at ₹1,108 premium, 2031 at discount.
lessons: A cumulative bond's fair value grows by accreted interest; early exit means accepting the market price.
Rising economy-wide rates push existing bond prices down and yields up; falling rates do the opposite.
Coupon is fixed on face value; yield is what the current price implies - they diverge as price moves.
Bond math is the transmission channel from central-bank policy to equity valuations.

summary: Q&A: 'waiting for the big correction' guarantees never investing (Nifty 12,400→7,500→15,000 arc); Maruti's call premium fell despite the stock rising because event-IV crushed after auto-sales data; retail gains conviction only at tops; why crowdfunding trading losses is morally wrong; Reliance re-rating thesis; short covering vs long unwinding in one line.
lessons: Waiting for the big correction means never investing: enter when you have money, exit when you need it.
Event IV inflates option prices pre-data and crushes after - right direction can still lose to volatility value.
Retail conviction peaks at market tops and bottoms out at market lows - the crowd is a contrarian map.
Trading losses are the trader's responsibility; expecting crowdfunding is greed dressed as need.
quotes: People seek certainty in an uncertain market - and that is the one thing it will never give.
Market 7,500 to 10,000: dead-cat bounce. To 12,500: valuation crash coming. To 14,000: FOMO. Above 15,000: now it is real - conviction arrives only at the top.

summary: Recovery week (3 sessions): Nifty regained ~14,900 after 14,260 low; S&P 500 crossed 4,000 first time; US payrolls +916k (7-month high). Feb–Mar correction measured −1,200 (15,450→14,260), two-thirds recovered; next magnet 15,450. RBI policy Wed (status quo expected). India VIX below 20 (2nd time in 2021). Range 14,500–15,200.
lessons: Fibonacci-style retracement logic: after two-thirds recovery, the prior high is the next magnet.
His max correction observed in a bull market: ~1,200 points — useful as a stress ruler, not a rule.

summary: No bank asks a restaurant loan-seeker for a 'stop loss'; businesses diagnose and fix (pricing, sourcing, menu) instead of pre-committing to a 2% shutdown. Mechanical stop-losses die by a thousand cuts in volatile markets; manage positions like a business, not a tripwire.
lessons: Nobody starts a business with a predetermined 'stop loss' - why should a trade, an ownership stake in a business, be any different?
In volatile markets, a stop hits before the move arrives; 1,000 small cuts (many small stops) kill an account as surely as one big loss.
A stop-loss is not a strategy: if it were, the 99% who religiously use stops would be winning.
Not using a stop does not mean riding losses: diagnose like a business owner - is it pricing, costs, or the thesis itself - then fix or exit deliberately.
quotes: If one cut of a knife can kill a person, a thousand small cuts can also kill.
Position sizing, stop loss, risk management - people talk of many things, but none of them will make you money by themselves.

summary: Tug-of-war day: bears dominated the morning, bulls the afternoon; Bank Nifty 2,000-point swing. Crisis-buying doctrine: buyers at Lehman and COVID troughs made >100% in a year (2011 Euro, 2013 taper, 2015 China, 2016 Brexit/demonetization/Trump, 2018 precedents). 14,250-15,450 labelled the 'ghost area' - write options only outside it.
lessons: Buying into every major crisis (Lehman, COVID) was rewarded with >100% within a year.
Define a 'ghost area' (prior high/low band) and only write options outside it.

summary: Election-day special: TMC landslide in West Bengal against exit polls; DMK leading TN. US barred Indian travellers from May 4; FII −₹3,500 cr Friday after rally to 15,050. April GST ₹1.41 lakh cr all-time record (+20% MoM) despite COVID. Sputnik V landed; 18–45 vaccination opened. Calls > puts now (14,800/15,000 walls). Range ~14,200–15,000.
lessons: A record tax collection during the worst health month is the economy's tell — separate the health cycle from the economy.
Sentiment flip visible in OI: unwinding 14,900/15,000 puts + adding 14,800–15,000 calls = resistance building into strength.

summary: US April payrolls +266k vs ~1M expected → 'very bad news is good news' rally (rate-hike odds down); SGX +120. India >4 lakh daily cases all week; TN 14-day lockdown from May 10. India VIX −10% in a week despite the record wave. OI: 14,500 PE max, 15,200 CE max. Range shift to 14,500–15,200; caution above 15,000.
lessons: Good news is good news; very good news is bad news; bad news is bad news; very bad news is good news — position by what the news does to policy expectations, not to the economy.
VIX falling into a catastrophe is a market-bottom signal: fear is peaking even as cases peak.

summary: Opened better than feared and recovered ~150 points; Bank Nifty +500-600 off lows; mid/small caps green while indices red. VIX closed below 20 for only the third 2021 session. Top five Nifty gainers were PSU banks. Both FIIs (-336cr) and DIIs sold ~1,000cr - 'who bought it?'
lessons: Option sellers must stay dynamic - roll the straddle to the new centre as the market drifts.
Be neither bull nor bear; be a chameleon - adapt positioning to the environment.

summary: Explains MTM and margin flow in options: buyer pays premium upfront and exits the picture; seller's margin = basic margin + premium. Premium received is cash in hand while the same amount is blocked as (collateral-funded) margin, so sellers effectively earn interest on premium received. As premium decays, blocked margin is released; adverse moves are still collateral-adjustable until exit.
lessons: Option buyer has no MTM; all daily settlement is between seller and exchange (exchange obligation, collateral-eligible) unlike futures' counterparty obligations (cash).
Premium received can earn interest because margin is collateral-funded - a quiet structural return for sellers.
Margin is dynamic: decaying premium releases blocked funds; losses top up margin without forced cash until booked.
quotes: Even if I lose money, I can still gain interest on that losing money.

summary: FII+DII sold ~3,000 crore over two days; FII index-futures long collapsed 70% to 40%. He exited all positions pre-CPI - the lose-5-to-save-200 asymmetry. Crowd uniformly bearish; 'markets bottom when the last bull turns bear'. PSU pack with dividend yields defied the fall. Support 14,580, resistance 14,780.
lessons: When everyone - cash, futures, options - is bearish, the market is often nearer a bottom than a breakdown.
Accept small certain losses (5-10 points) to avoid large uncertain ones; sleep is a position too.
